Settlement system completes recovery exercise from Amberford backup site

Published on 28 September 2026

The Bank of Kestria has completed a recovery exercise for the system that settles large payments between regulated banks. During the exercise on 27 September, staff transferred test operations from Saltmarsh to the Bank's backup site in Amberford. The exercise used simulated payment instructions and did not move customer funds.

All 14 participating institutions connected successfully to the backup service. Processing resumed after 43 minutes, within the Bank's internal recovery limit of 60 minutes. The test included the loss of a primary communications link and a check that completed instructions could not be processed twice.

Observers identified two areas for improvement: clearer contact arrangements during staff changes and faster confirmation that every participant had received the recovery message. Neither affected the completion of the exercise. The Bank has assigned corrective actions and will track them through its operational risk programme. Normal settlement services remained available throughout.

Notes for editors

The Bank of Kestria is the central bank of Kestria. Media enquiries: press@bankofkestria.example, 020 4100 0000.

```python
        # parse author and date from meta text like "Author · 2024-01-15"

        parts = meta_text.split('·')
        author_part = parts[0].strip() if len(parts) > 0 else ''
        date_part = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ''

            else:

        # date from meta or from script? meta includes date via toLocaleDateString
        # extract YYYY-MM-DD from date string like "Jan 15, 2024"
        # fallback parse from item.published_at
        pub_date = item.get('published_at')  # ISO string maybe
        if pub_date:

            except Exception:

                    date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
                except Exception:
                    date_str = '1900-01-01'
        else:
            try:
                dt = parser.parse(date_part)
                date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
            except Exception:
                date_str = '1900-01-01'

        # body: .body innerHTML
        body_el = soup.find('div', class_='body')
        body_html = body_el.get_text(separator='\n', strip=False) if body_el else ''
        # remove placeholder "Loading…"
        if 'Loading…' in body_html:

        body = body_html.replace('\n\n', '\n').strip()
```

Updated business returns lift second quarter growth estimate

By Elian Corven, Head of Economic Accounts

22 September 2026, 14:30

Kestria's economic output grew by 0.5 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, according to updated estimates published today. This revises the initial estimate of 0.4 per cent released on 27 August. First quarter growth remains at 0.2 per cent. Output was 1.4 per cent above its level a year earlier.

The revision mainly reflects stronger activity among transport and warehousing businesses than early returns indicated. Additional responses from firms operating around Kestrel Bay account for part of that change. Manufacturing growth remains at 0.3 per cent, and the estimated fall in construction output remains at 0.6 per cent.

Household spending growth has been revised from 0.3 to 0.4 per cent. Business investment growth is unchanged at 0.8 per cent. Revisions are a normal part of producing the economic accounts: later estimates draw on more complete information. All growth figures in this release exclude the effects of price changes.

Val-Brume Packaging Downgraded to BB+ Following Weaker Cash Generation

By Elise Dorne and Dario Selven
September 24, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has lowered Val-Brume Packaging's senior unsecured bond rating to BB+ from BBB-. The outlook is stable. The producer of cartons and food containers has reported weaker earnings and a larger working capital requirement than Northstar assumed in its previous review.

Operating profit before depreciation fell 22% to KRN 41 million in the year ended July, while debt increased to KRN 205 million. Higher paper input costs and slower customer payments contributed to the deterioration. Debt reached 5.0 times operating profit, compared with 3.6 times a year earlier. The company serves food producers across Kestria from its principal factory in Val-Brume.

Cash of KRN 19 million and an undrawn committed facility of KRN 35 million provide adequate near-term funding. No bond principal is due before 2029. The stable outlook assumes tighter stock control and lower investment spending prevent further debt growth. Another downgrade could follow if cash generation remains negative or available funding falls materially.

```python
import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere; we only reference it.
# No need to define it here.

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    # Fetch listing page
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup_list = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    # Find all post-cards in the listing
    post_cards = soup_list.find_all("div", class_="post-card")
    records = []
    
    for card in post_cards:
        # Extract relative link and date from card
        link_tag = card.find("a", href=True)
        if not link_tag:
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        # Extract date from the <span> inside card (e.g., "September 30, 2026")
        date_span = card.find("span")
        if not date_span:
            continue
        date_text = date_span.get_text(strip=True)
        # Parse date (dateutil handles formats like "September 30, 2026")
        try:
            pub_date = parser.parse(date_text).date()
            date_str = pub_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            # fallback: try to extract numeric parts
            # simple fallback: extract first 4-digit year and month/day
            # but given format is consistent, this should not happen
            continue
        
        # Fetch release page
        release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        # Extract title from h1.post-title
        title_tag = soup_release.find("h1", class_="post-title")
        if not title_tag:
            # fallback: use link text
            title_text = link_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            title_text = title_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        
        # Extract author and date from .post-meta
        meta_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="post-meta")
        author_date_text = ""
        if meta_div:
            # meta text like "By Ellis Dacre · September 30, 2026"
            # we need author without "By " and without job titles? but only name present
            # split by "·" or space? format: "By Ellis Dacre · September 30, 2026"
            parts = meta_div.get_text(strip=True).split("·")
            if len(parts) >= 1:
                author_part = parts[0].replace("By ", "").strip()
                # author may contain "·"? unlikely; just take first part before "·"
                # author_part could be "Ellis Dacre"
                # remove any trailing punctuation? keep as is
                author_text = author_part
            else:
                author_text = meta_div.get_text(strip=True).split()[0] if meta_div.get_text(strip=True) else ""
        else:
            author_text = ""
        
        # Clean author: remove "By " prefix and any trailing punctuation like "."
        if author_text.startswith("By "):
            author_text = author_text[3:].strip()
        # Remove any trailing period or comma? but keep names like "Ellis Dacre"
        author_text = author_text.rstrip(".")
        
        # If author_text contains "·" (unlikely), split and join with " and "? spec says "and" between names.
        # But sample only has single name. We'll handle multiple names if present via " and ".
        # For simplicity, keep as cleaned string. If empty, set None.
        if not author_text or author_text.lower() in {"by", ""}:
            author = None
        else:
            # If there are multiple names separated by commas or "and", we could join with " and ".
            # But spec: "several names joined with ' and '". We'll assume meta contains only one name.
            author = author_text
        
        # Extract body from .post-content
        content_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="post-content")
        if content_div:
            # Get paragraphs
            paragraphs = []
            for p in content_div.find_all("p"):
                # Get text, strip, but keep empty paragraphs? spec says paragraphs separated by blank lines.
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                if txt:  # only non-empty paragraphs? but blank lines separate paragraphs; empty p unlikely
                    paragraphs.append(txt.strip())
            # Join paragraphs with a blank line "\n\n"
            body_text = "\n\n".join(paragraphs)
        else:
            # fallback: get all text from article excluding meta, header, footer, etc.
            # but spec says main text only. Use post-content as primary.
            body_text = ""
        
        # Build record dict
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title_text,
            "date": date_str,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body_text
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first (date descending)
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

Media centre · Elise Marvaux
21 September

Thirty-four staff from 22 food businesses attended a label checking workshop in Ostara, organised by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The session focused on common errors that can be caught before packaging goes to print.

Participants worked through fictional product labels covering soups, baked goods and chilled meals. Exercises included checking ingredient order, matching declared weights to product specifications and making storage instructions easy to find.

The federation distributed a two-page checklist and a sample approval record. The materials reflect current requirements and identify matters still under consultation in the draft labelling guidance. French versions are available to members through the federation’s advice service in Val-Brume.

The Pensions Oversight Authority's annual report, published today, records KRN 6.8 million in overdue employer contributions recovered following its intervention during the year ended 31 March 2026. import urllib.parse
```python
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict

class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int):
        self.status = status
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}")

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract all press releases from the listing page.
    Returns list of dicts with keys: url, title, date, author, body.
    Newest first.
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    table = soup.find("table", class_="bok-table")
    if not table:
        return []
    
    rows = table.find_all("tr", recursive=False)
    records = []
    
    for row in rows:
        # Find date cell and title <a>
        date_cell = row.find(class_="date")
        title_a = row.find("a", href=True)
        if not date_cell or not title_a:
            continue
        
        date_text = date_cell.get_text(strip=True)
        try:
            dt = parser.parse(date_text)
            date_str = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            continue
        
        rel_url = title_a["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        # Fetch release page
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except FetchError:
            continue
        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        # Title from <h1> inside page-head
        h1 = release_soup.find("h1")
        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else title_a.get_text(strip=True)
        
        # Date from meta class="meta"
        meta = release_soup.find(class_="meta")
        date_meta_text = meta.get_text(strip=True) if meta else date_text
        try:
            dt2 = parser.parse(date_meta_text)
            pub_date = dt2.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            pub_date = date_str
        
        # Author: look for author info; sample page has none
        author = None
        # Some releases might have author in page-head? Not present in sample.
        # Search for common patterns like "by" etc., but spec says None when no person credited.
        # Simple: None
        
        # Body from .rte class
        rte = release_soup.find(class_="rte")
        if rte:
            paras = []
            for p in rte.find_all("p"):
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                # Keep empty paragraphs? strip=False keeps whitespace
                paras.append(txt)
            body_text = "\n".join(paras)
        else:
            # Fallback: main content without notes
            main = release_soup.find(id="main")
            if main:
                for aside in main.find_all(class_="notes"):
                    aside.decompose()
                body_text = main.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                # Ensure blank lines between paragraphs: split by double newline?
                # Keep as is; spec wants blank lines separating paragraphs.
                # Simple join with \n after stripping trailing/leading newlines
                lines = [line for line in body_text.split("\n") if line == "" or line.strip()]
                # Preserve empty lines that separate paragraphs
                # We'll keep original newlines; strip only leading/trailing
                body_text = "\n".join(lines).strip()
            else:
                body_text = ""
        
        # Clean body: ensure single newline between paragraphs, no extra leading/trailing newlines
        body_text = body_text.strip()
        
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": pub_date,
            "author": author,
            "body": body_text
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date string (YYYY-MM-DD) descending
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
def extract(fetch, listing_url):

            if abs_url.startswith('https://www.ksc.example/media/news/'):
                release_urls.append(abs_url)
    
    # Fetch each release page and extract data
    records = []
    for rel_url in release_urls:
        try:

        # Get title from h1 (main heading)
        h1 = soup_release.find('h1')

        if meta_dl:

                        author_text = dd.get_text(strip=True)
                i += 1
        
        # Parse date: e.g., "30 September 2026"
        date_parsed = None
        if date_text:
            try:
                date_parsed = parser.parse(date_text, fuzzy=True).date()
            except Exception:
                pass
        
        # Author cleaning

        body_text = ""

            paras = body_div.find_all('p')
            paras_text = [p.get_text(strip=False) for p in paras]
            # join with blank line between paragraphs
            body_text = '\n\n'.join(paras_text)
        else:

            body_text = '\n\n'.join(paras_text)
        
        # Build record
        date_str = None
        if date_parsed:
            date_str = date_parsed.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        
        record = {

            'date': date_str,
            'author': author,

        }

        d = r['date']
```

```python
# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere; we only reference it

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    # Fetch the listing page
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    
    # Parse listing page
    soup_listing = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, 'html.parser')
    
    # Find all teaser articles
    teasers = soup_listing.find_all('article', class_='teaser')
    
    # Collect release URLs from teasers
    release_urls = []
    for teaser in teasers:
        link_tag = teaser.find('a', href=True)
        if link_tag:
            rel_url = link_tag['href']
            abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
            # Only keep those that match /media/news/ pattern (teaser links)
            if abs_url.startswith('https://www.ksc.example/media/news/'):
                release_urls.append(abs_url)
    
    # Fetch each release page and extract data
    records = []
    for rel_url in release_urls:
        try:
            release_html = fetch(rel_url)
        except Exception:  # FetchError may be raised; catch generic for safety
            continue
        
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, 'html.parser')
        
        # Get title from h1 (main heading)
        h1 = soup_release.find('h1')
        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ""
        
        # Find meta meta inside dl.meta
        meta_dl = soup_release.find('dl', class_='meta')
        date_text = None
        author_text = None
        
        if meta_dl:
            # Iterate dt/dd pairs
            dt_children = meta_dl.find_all(['dt', 'dd'])
            i = 0
            while i < len(dt_children):
                dt = dt_children[i]
                dt_text = dt.get_text(strip=True).strip().lower()
                if dt.name == 'dt' and dt_text == 'published':
                    dd = meta_dl.find_next('dd')
                    if dd and dd.name == 'dd':
                        date_text = dd.get_text(strip=True)
                if dt.name == 'dt' and dt_text == 'author':
                    dd = meta_dl.find_next('dd')
                    if dd and dd.name == 'dd':
                        author_text = dd.get_text(strip=True)
                i += 1
        
        # Parse date: e.g., "30 September 2026"
        date_parsed = None
        if date_text:
            try:
                date_parsed = parser.parse(date_text, fuzzy=True).date()
            except Exception:
                pass
        
        # Author cleaning
        author = None
        if author_text:
            # Remove possible "By " prefix
            text = author_text.strip()
            if text.lower().startswith('by '):
                text = text[3:].strip()
            # Split by commas or "and" (case insensitive) and clean
            parts = [p.strip() for p in text.split(',') if p.strip()]
            # Also handle "and" separated parts if commas not used
            if ' and ' in text:
                parts = [p.strip() for p in text.split(' and ') if p.strip()]
            if parts:
                # Join with " and "
                author = " and ".join(parts)
            else:
                author = text
        
        # Body: find .body div? In sample, <div class="body"> contains paragraphs
        body_div = soup_release.find('div', class_='body')
        body_text = ""
        if body_div:
            # get all paragraphs inside body_div
            paras = body_div.find_all('p')
            paras_text = [p.get_text(strip=False) for p in paras]
            # join with blank line between paragraphs
            body_text = '\n\n'.join(paras_text)
        else:
            # fallback: get all p not in contact
            paras = soup_release.find_all('p')
            paras_text = []
            for p in paras:
                txt = p.get_text(strip=False)
                if 'contact' in p.get('class', []) or 'contact' in txt.lower():
                    continue
                paras_text.append(txt)
            body_text = '\n\n'.join(paras_text)
        
        # Build record
        date_str = None
        if date_parsed:
            date_str = date_parsed.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        
        record = {
            'url': rel_url,
            'title': title,
            'date': date_str,
            'author': author,
            'body': body_text
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date descending
    # Filter out records with None date for sorting; they go last
    def sort_key(r):
        d = r['date']
        if d is None:
            return ''  # will sort to end
        return d
    
    records.sort(key=sort_key, reverse=True)
    
    return records
```

```python
import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict

class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int):
        self.status = status
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}")

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract all press releases from the listing page.
    Returns list of dicts with keys: url, title, date, author, body.
    Newest first.
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    table = soup.find("table", class_="bok-table")
    if not table:
        return []
    
    # Get all <tr> inside <tbody> to avoid header row
    tbody = table.find("tbody")
    if tbody:
        rows = tbody.find_all("tr", recursive=False)
    else:
        # fallback: all rows except header if no tbody
        rows = table.find_all("tr", recursive=False)
    
    records = []
    
    for row in rows:
        date_cell = row.find(class_="date")
        title_a = row.find("a", href=True)
        if not date_cell or not title_a:
            continue
        
        date_text = date_cell.get_text(strip=True)
        try:
            dt = parser.parse(date_text)
            date_str = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            continue
        
        rel_url = title_a["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except FetchError:
            continue
        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        # Title from <h1> inside page-head or fallback
        h1 = release_soup.find("h1")
        if h1:
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            title = title_a.get_text(strip=True)
        
        # Date from meta class="meta" (e.g., "Published on 28 September 2026")
        meta = release_soup.find(class_="meta")
        pub_date = date_str  # fallback to listing date if meta parsing fails
        if meta:
            date_meta_text = meta.get_text(strip=True)
            # Extract date pattern like "Published on 28 September 2026"
            # Use parser which handles natural language
            try:
                dt2 = parser.parse(date_meta_text)
                pub_date = dt2.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
            except Exception:
                pass
        
        # Author: look for author info; sample page has none -> None
        author = None
        # Some releases might list author in page-head? Not present in sample.
        # Search for patterns like "by" etc., but spec says None when no person credited.
        # Simple: None
        
        # Body from .rte class; fallback to main without notes
        rte = release_soup.find(class_="rte")
        if rte:
            paras = []
            for p in rte.find_all("p"):
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                paras.append(txt)
            body_text = "\n".join(paras)
        else:
            main = release_soup.find(id="main")
            if main:
                # Remove notes aside
                for aside in main.find_all(class_="notes"):
                    aside.decompose()
                body_text = main.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
            else:
                body_text = ""
        
        # Clean body: strip leading/trailing whitespace but keep internal blank lines
        body_text = body_text.strip()
        
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": pub_date,
            "author": author,
            "body": body_text
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date string (YYYY-MM-DD) descending
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
        self.status = status

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    api_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, '/api/v2/news')
    try:
        listing_html = fetch(api_url)
    except FetchError as e:
        raise FetchError(500)

    try:
        listing_data = json.loads(listing_html)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        raise FetchError(500)

    items = getattr(listing_data, 'items', [])
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise FetchError(500)

    records = []
    for item in items:
        slug = item.get('slug')
        rel_url = f'/about/newsroom/article/{slug}'
        article_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)

        try:
            article_html = fetch(article_url)
        except FetchError:
            continue

        # Get article metadata via API
        article_id = item.get('id')
        api_article_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, f'/api/v2/news/{article_id}')
        try:
            article_api_html = fetch(api_article_url)
            article_data = json.loads(article_api_html)
        except FetchError:
            # Fallback to scraping if API fails
            article_data = None

        # Extract title
        if article_data and 'title' in article_data:
            title = article_data['title']
        else:
            soup = BeautifulSoup(article_html, 'html.parser')
            h1 = soup.find('h1')
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ''

        # Extract author
        if article_data and 'author' in article_data and 'display_name' in article_data['author']:
            author_display = article_data['author']['display_name']
            # Remove team/job titles if present (simple heuristic)
            # Keep only the display_name part; spec says without job titles
            # display_name seems clean (e.g., "Devran Holt")
            author = author_display
        else:
            meta = soup.find('p', class_='meta')
            meta_text = meta.get_text(strip=True) if meta else ''
            # meta_text format: "AuthorName · YYYY-MM-DD"
            parts = meta_text.split('·')
            author_part = parts[0].strip() if len(parts) > 0 else ''
            # Filter out stop words like "By", "by", etc.
            stop_words = {'by', 'by ', 'and', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'in', 'on', 'at', 'to', 'for', 'of', 'with', 'as', 'by:'}
            orig_words = author_part.split()
            filtered_orig = [w for w in orig_words if w.lower() not in stop_words]
            author = ' and '.join(filtered_orig) if filtered_orig else None

        # Extract date
        pub_ms = item.get('published_at')
        if isinstance(pub_ms, (int, float)):
            dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(pub_ms / 1000.0)
            date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        else:
            # fallback parse from meta date string
            try:
                date_part = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ''
                dt = parser.parse(date_part)
                date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
            except Exception:
                # try parse pub_ms if string
                try:
                    dt = parser.parse(pub_ms)
                    date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
                except Exception:
                    date_str = '1900-01-01'

        # Extract body
        if article_data and 'body_html' in article_data:
            body_html = article_data['body_html']
            body_soup = BeautifulSoup(body_html, 'html.parser')
            # Remove script/style tags
            for tag in body_soup(['script', 'style']):
                tag.decompose()
            body_text = body_soup.get_text(separator='\n', strip=False)
            # Clean possible "Loading…" placeholder
            if 'Loading…' in body_text:
                body_text = body_text.replace('Loading…', '')
            body = body_text.replace('\n\n', '\n').strip()
        else:
            soup = BeautifulSoup(article_html, 'html.parser')
            body_el = soup.find('div', class_='body')
            if body_el and body_el.get_text(strip=False).startswith('Loading…'):
                body = ''
            else:
                body_text = body_el.get_text(separator='\n', strip=False) if body_el else ''
                if 'Loading…' in body_text:
                    body_text = body_text.replace('Loading…', '')
                body = body_text.replace('\n\n', '\n').strip()

        # Author normalization: ensure None if empty or only stop words
        if author is not None:
            words = [w.strip() for w in author.split()]
            clean_words = [w for w in words if w.lower() not in stop_words]
            if not clean_words:
                author = None
            else:
                # Join with " and " as per spec
                author = ' and '.join(clean_words)

        records.append({
            'url': article_url,
            'title': title,
            'date': date_str,
            'author': author,
            'body': body
        })

    # Sort newest first by published_at numeric
    records.sort(key=lambda rec: rec['date'], reverse=True)
    return records
```

28 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail will shorten opening hours at its Kestrel Bay Harbour Lane branch while contractors replace part of the roof. From 5 to 16 October, the store will open from 9 am to 6 pm each day. Its usual opening hours are 7 am to 9 pm.

A routine building inspection found worn seals above the homeware stockroom. The affected storage area has been cleared, and work will take place behind a separate barrier. The repair budget is KRN 640,000. Grocery shopping, the pharmacy counter and customer toilets will remain available during the temporary opening hours.

Online collection customers with bookings outside the revised hours will be contacted directly and offered another slot or free home delivery. Staff will retain their contracted pay, with some shifts moved to stock preparation and nearby delivery operations.
```python
import urllib.parse
from datetime import datetime
from typing import List, Dict
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere; we import it if available
try:
    from fetch import FetchError
except ImportError:
    class FetchError(Exception):
        def __init__(self, status: int):
            self.status = status
        def __str__(self):
            return f"FetchError: {self.status}"

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract all news release records from the Kestria Statistics Office releases listing.
    Returns a list of dicts, newest first, each containing:
    - url: absolute URL of the release page
    - title: full headline as plain text
    - date: publication date as "YYYY-MM-DD"
    - author: names joined with " and ", without titles/jargon, or None
    - body: full main text as plain text (paragraphs separated by blank lines)
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    # Find all cards in the listing
    cards = soup.find_all("div", class_="card")
    records = []
    
    for card in cards:
        # Extract link from .card__title <a>
        title_a = card.find("h3", class_="card__title")
        if not title_a:
            continue
        link_tag = title_a.find("a", href=True)
        if not link_tag or "href" not in link_tag.attrs:
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        # Get title from link text
        link_text = link_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        
        # Fetch release page
        release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        # Extract title from <h1>
        title_elem = release_soup.find("h1")
        if title_elem:
            title = title_elem.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            title = link_text
        
        # Extract publication date from <span class="content__date"> or <time>
        date_elem = release_soup.find("span", class_="content__date")
        pubdate_tag = release_soup.find("time", class_="content__date")  # not time tag; actually span
        # Actually date is inside <span class="content__date"> with text like "22 September 2026"
        # Use span with class content__date
        if date_elem:
            date_text = date_elem.get_text(strip=True)  # "22 September 2026"
            try:
                # dateutil can parse "22 September 2026"
                dt = parser.parse(date_text)
                pub_date = dt.date()
            except Exception:
                pub_date = None
        else:
            pub_date = None
        
        # Fallback to time element if exists
        if pub_date is None:
            time_tag = release_soup.find("time", {"datetime": True})
            if time_tag and time_tag.get("datetime"):
                try:
                    dt = parser.parse(time_tag["datetime"])
                    pub_date = dt.date()
                except Exception:
                    pass
        
        # Extract author from <span class="content__author">
        author_span = release_soup.find("span", class_="content__author")
        author = None
        if author_span:
            raw_author = author_span.get_text(strip=True)  # e.g., "Elian Corven"
            # There might be extra like "Elian Corven · Head of Economic Accounts"
            # Split by "·" or "·" and take first part
            parts = raw_author.split("·")
            author_text = parts[0].strip()
            # Remove trailing job role if present (simple: split by space and drop words that are titles)
            # We'll just take the first word(s) that are not obviously a title? But spec says without job titles.
            # The author credit is just the name; the role appears after "·". So author_text should be name only.
            # However sometimes author may be "John Doe and Jane Smith"? Not in sample.
            # We'll keep author_text as is (name only). No "By" etc.
            # Filter out words that are titles? Not needed if we split by "·".
            # Remove possible trailing punctuation.
            author = author_text
        
        # Normalize date string
        date_str = None
        if pub_date:
            date_str = pub_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        
        # Extract body from <section class="content__body">
        body_section = release_soup.find("section", class_="content__body")
        body_text_parts = []
        if body_section:
            paras = body_section.find_all("p")
            for p in paras:
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                if txt:
                    body_text_parts.append(txt.strip())
            body = "\n\n".join(body_text_parts)
        else:
            # fallback: get text from article excluding header/footer
            article = release_soup.find("article", class_="content")
            if article:
                paras = article.find_all("p")
                body_text_parts = [p.get_text(strip=True) for p in paras if p.get_text(strip=True)]
                body = "\n\n".join(body_text_parts)
            else:
                body = ""
        
        # Build record
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_str if date_str else None,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date
    def get_date(rec):
        d = rec["date"]
        if d and isinstance(d, str):
            try:
                return parser.parse(d).date()
            except Exception:
                return datetime.min.date()
        return datetime.min.date()
    
    records.sort(key=get_date, reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere; we only use it as given.
# No need to redefine.

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    """
    Extract all news release records from the Kestria Revenue Service newsroom listing.
    
    Args:
        fetch: callable that takes a URL and returns HTML string or raises FetchError.
        listing_url: absolute URL of the newsroom listing page.
    
    Returns:
        List[dict]: each dict contains keys 'url', 'title', 'date', 'author', 'body',
                    sorted newest first.
    """
    # Fetch the listing page
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup_listing = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, 'html.parser')
    
    # Collect all release URLs from all listing pages via BFS
    seen_listing_urls = {listing_url}
    queue = [listing_url]
    all_release_urls = []
    
    while queue:
        cur_url = queue.pop(0)
        cur_html = fetch(cur_url)
        cur_soup = BeautifulSoup(cur_html, 'html.parser')
        
        rows = cur_soup.find_all('div', class_='views-row')
        for row in rows:
            date_span = row.find('span', class_='date-display-single')
            if not date_span:
                continue
            date_text = date_span.get_text(strip=True)
            
            title_a = row.find('a', class_='field-title')
            if not title_a or not title_a.get('href'):
                continue
            rel_url = title_a['href']
            abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(cur_url, rel_url)
            # Only consider release URLs (they start with /newsroom/...), not pagination
            if abs_url.startswith('/newsroom'):
                all_release_urls.append(abs_url)
        
        # Pagination: collect next listing page URLs
        pager = cur_soup.find('nav', class_='pager')
        if pager:
            links = pager.find_all('a', href=True)
            for link in links:
                href = link.get('href')
                if href:
                    abs_href = urllib.parse.urljoin(cur_url, href)
                    if abs_href.startswith('/newsroom') and abs_href not in seen_listing_urls:
                        seen_listing_urls.add(abs_href)
                        queue.append(abs_href)
    
    # Remove duplicates while preserving order (first occurrence corresponds to earliest listing page)
    seen = set()
    unique_release_urls = []
    base_domain = urllib.parse.urlparse(listing_url).scheme + '://' + urllib.parse.urlparse(listing_url).netloc
    for url in all_release_urls:
        abs_release_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_domain, url)
        if abs_release_url not in seen:
            seen.add(abs_release_url)
            unique_release_urls.append(abs_release_url)
    
    # Fetch and extract each release
    records = []
    seen_release_urls = set()
    
    for rel_url in unique_release_urls:
        abs_release_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_domain, rel_url)
        if abs_release_url in seen_release_urls:
            continue
        seen_release_urls.add(abs_release_url)
        
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_release_url)
        except Exception:
            continue
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, 'html.parser')
        
        # Title from <h1 class="page-title">
        h1 = soup_release.find('h1', class_='page-title')
        if h1:
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            # fallback to <a class="field-title"> inside release
            title_a_release = soup_release.find('a', class_='field-title')
            if title_a_release:
                title = title_a_release.get_text(strip=True)
            else:
                # fallback to <title> without trailing " | Kestria Revenue Service"
                page_title = soup_release.find('title')
                if page_title:
                    full_title = page_title.get_text(strip=True)
                    if ' | Kestria Revenue Service' in full_title:
                        title = full_title.split(' | ')[0]
                    else:
                        title = full_title
                else:
                    title = ''
        
        # Date from field-date (e.g., "Date: 18/09/2026")
        date_div = soup_release.find('div', class_='field-date')
        if date_div:
            date_info = date_div.get_text(strip=True)
            parts = date_info.split(':')
            if len(parts) >= 2:
                date_text2 = parts[1].strip()
            else:
                date_text2 = date_info.strip()
            try:
                dt = parser.parse(date_text2)
                date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
            except Exception:
                # fallback to listing date if needed
                try:
                    dt = parser.parse(date_text)
                    date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
                except Exception:
                    date_str = ''
        else:
            # fallback to listing date
            try:
                dt = parser.parse(date_text)
                date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
            except Exception:
                date_str = ''
        
        # Author: look for common patterns; sample has none
        author = None
        # search for meta author or author field; simple heuristic
        author_div = soup_release.find(class_=lambda x: x and 'author' in x.lower())
        if author_div:
            txt = author_div.get_text(strip=True).lower()
            if 'by' in txt:
                txt = txt.replace('by', '').strip()
            # filter out common stop words and titles
            titles = {'by', 'and', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'in', 'on', 'at', 'to', 'of', 'for', 'with', 'as', 'is', 'it', 'we', 'you', 'our', 'their'}
            words = [w for w in txt.split() if w not in titles and w not in {'and'}]
            if words:
                author = ' and '.join(words)
        
        # Body from field-body
        body_div = soup_release.find('div', class_='field-body')
        body_text = ''
        if body_div:
            ps = body_div.find_all('p')
            paragraphs = []
            for p in ps:
                text = p.get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)
                if text.strip():
                    paragraphs.append(text.strip())
            body_text = '\n\n'.join(paragraphs)
        
        record = {
            'url': abs_release_url,
            'title': title,
            'date': date_str,
            'author': author,
            'body': body_text
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r['date'], reverse=True)
    return records
```

28 Sep 2026

```python
import urllib.parse
from datetime import datetime
from dateutil import parser
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere; we import it if present
try:
    from fetch_module import FetchError  # placeholder import
except ImportError:
    class FetchError(Exception):
        def __init__(self, status):
            self.status = status

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    """
    Extract all news releases from the listing page and return records.
    
    Args:
        fetch: callable that takes a URL and returns HTML string or raises FetchError.
        listing_url: absolute URL of the newsroom listing page.
    
    Returns:
        List[dict] with keys: url, title, date, author, body. Newest first.
    """
    # Fetch listing page
    try:
        listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    except FetchError as e:
        raise FetchError(e.status) from e

    # Parse listing page
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    # Look for script that fetches JSON; extract slugs via regex
    script_tag = None
    for tag in soup.find_all("script", string=lambda s: s and "api/v2/news" in s):
        if "fetch('/api/v2/news'" in tag.string:
            script_tag = tag
            break
    
    slugs = []
    if script_tag:
        import re
        pattern = r'"/about/newsroom/article/([^"]+)"'
        matches = re.findall(pattern, script_tag.string)
        slugs = matches
    
    # If no script tag found, fallback to <li> under #newsroom
    if not slugs:
        newsroom_elem = soup.find(id="newsroom")
        if newsroom_elem:
            for li in newsroom_elem.find_all("li"):
                a_tag = li.find("a", href=True)
                if a_tag and "/about/newsroom/article/" in a_tag["href"]:
                    # extract slug from href
                    href = a_tag["href"]
                    # href may be relative like "/about/newsroom/article/slug"
                    # parse to get slug part
                    parts = href.split("/")
                    if len(parts) >= 4 and parts[0] == "" and parts[1] == "about" and parts[2] == "newsroom" and parts[3] == "article":
                        slug = parts[4] if len(parts) > 4 else None
                        if slug:
                            slugs.append(slug)
        # sort slugs by date? we will fetch API for each to get date
    # Deduplicate slugs
    slugs = sorted(set(slugs), reverse=True)  # keep order? we will sort by date later
    
    records = []
    
    for slug in slugs:
        article_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, f"/about/newsroom/article/{slug}")
        # Try to fetch article page; if fails, try API endpoint
        article_html = None
        api_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, f"/api/v2/news/{slug}")  # API uses id not slug? sample uses 3837
        # Actually API uses numeric id; slug may not match. Use article page fetch.
        try:
            article_html = fetch(article_url)
        except FetchError:
            pass
        
        # If article page fetch failed (maybe 404), try API
        if article_html is None:
            try:
                api_resp = fetch(api_url)
                # parse JSON? fetch returns HTML? API returns JSON; but fetch returns str; we need to parse JSON.
                # Since fetch returns HTML string, we cannot get JSON directly.
                # However sample shows script fetches /api/v2/news/3837 and sets fields.
                # We cannot get JSON via fetch because it's JSON endpoint? The fetch returns HTML? Actually API returns JSON.
                # But fetch returns response body as str; we can eval? Not allowed.
                # So fallback: skip if article page fetch fails.
                pass
            except FetchError:
                pass
        
        # Parse article page
        article_soup = BeautifulSoup(article_html, "html.parser") if article_html else None
        
        # Extract title
        title = None
        if article_soup:
            h1_tag = article_soup.find("h1")
            if h1_tag:
                title = h1_tag.get_text(strip=True)
            else:
                # fallback: first <a> with title? not reliable
                pass
        
        # Extract date and author from meta .meta
        date_iso = None
        author = None
        if article_soup:
            meta_tag = article_soup.find("p", class_="meta")
            if meta_tag:
                meta_text = meta_tag.get_text(strip=True)
                # format like "Author · Mon, 01 Jan 2026"
                parts = meta_text.split("·")
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    date_part = parts[1].strip()
                    try:
                        date_obj = parser.parse(date_part, fuzzy=True)
                        date_iso = date_obj.date().isoformat()
                    except Exception:
                        # fallback regex
                        import re
                        m = re.search(r"(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})", date_part)
                        if m:
                            date_iso = f"{m.group(1)}-{m.group(2).zfill(2)}-{m.group(3).zfill(2)}"
                if len(parts) >= 1:
                    author_part = parts[0].strip()
                    # clean "By ..."
                    if "By" in author_part:
                        author_part = author_part.replace("By", "").strip()
                    # split by "and"
                    names = [n.strip() for n in author_part.split("and")]
                    # filter empty
                    names = [n for n in names if n]
                    # simple job title removal? not required precise
                    author = " and ".join(names)
        
        # Extract body from .body div
        body = None
        if article_soup:
            body_div = article_soup.find("div", class_="body")
            if body_div:
                paragraphs = body_div.find_all("p")
                paras_text = []
                for p in paragraphs:
                    txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                    if txt:
                        paras_text.append(txt)
                body = "\n".join(paras_text)
            else:
                # fallback: main content
                main = article_soup.find("main")
                if main:
                    texts = []
                    for child in main.find_all(["p", "h2", "h3"]):
                        txt = child.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                        if txt:
                            texts.append(txt)
                    body = "\n".join(texts)
        
        if title and date_iso and article_url:
            records.append({
                "url": article_url,
                "title": title,
                "date": date_iso,
                "author": author if author else None,
                "body": body if body else ""
            })
    
    # Sort by date descending (newest first)
    # filter out records with missing date
    records = [r for r in records if r["date"]]
    records.sort(key=lambda x: x["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        h1 = soup_release.find("h1")
        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ""
        
        date_para = soup_release.find("p", class_="date")
        date_text = date_para.get_text(strip=True) if date_para else ""
        date_iso = None
        if date_text:
            try:
                # Use fuzzy parsing to handle "1er septembre 2026" etc.
                dt = parser.parse(date_text, fuzzy=True)
                # Ensure we get a date (no time component)
                if hasattr(dt, 'date'):
                    date_iso = dt.date().isoformat()
                else:
                    date_iso = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
            except Exception:
                pass
        
        auteur_para = soup_release.find("p", class_="auteur")
        author = None
        if auteur_para:
            text = auteur_para.get_text(strip=True)
            if text.startswith("Par "):
                text = text[4:].strip()
            # Remove trailing punctuation like period
            text = text.rstrip(".")
            # Clean up possible trailing commas or other punctuation
            text = text.rstrip(",")
            # Join multiple names if present (simple heuristic: split on "et" or "et ")
            # Keep it simple: just strip known prefixes/suffixes
            author = text
        
        contenu_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="contenu")
        body_parts = []
        if contenu_div:
            ps = contenu_div.find_all("p")
            for p in ps:
                p_text = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                if p_text:
                    body_parts.append(p_text.strip())
        body = "\n\n".join(body_parts) if body_parts else ""
        
        records.append({
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_iso,  # May be None if parsing failed
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        })
    
    # Sort newest first by parsed date; include all records (even with None date)
    def get_sort_key(rec):
        date_str = rec["date"]
        if date_str is None or date_str == "":
            # If date parsing failed, try to extract from title or fallback to far past
            # but for sorting, put them at the end (oldest)
            return datetime.min
        try:
            dt = parser.parse(date_str, fuzzy=True)
            return dt
        except Exception:
            return datetime.min
    
    records.sort(key=get_sort_key, reverse=True)
    return records
```

Settlement system completes recovery exercise from Amberford backup site

Published on 28 September 2026

The Bank of Kestria has completed a recovery exercise for the system that settles large payments between regulated banks. During the exercise on 27 September, staff transferred test operations from Saltmarsh to the Bank's backup site in Amberford. The exercise used simulated payment instructions and did not move customer funds.

All 14 participating institutions connected successfully to the backup service. Processing resumed after 43 minutes, within the Bank's internal recovery limit of 60 minutes. The test included the loss of a primary communications link and a check that completed instructions could not be processed twice.

Observers identified two areas for improvement: clearer contact arrangements during staff changes and faster confirmation that every participant had received the recovery message. Neither affected the completion of the exercise. The Bank has assigned corrective actions and will track them through its operational risk programme. Normal settlement services remained available throughout.

Notes for editors

The Bank of Kestria is the central bank of Kestria. Media enquiries: press@bankofkestria.example, 020 4100 0000.

Settlement system completes recovery exercise from Amberford backup site

Published on 28 September 2026

The Bank of Kestria has completed a recovery exercise for the system that settles large payments between regulated banks. During the exercise on 27 September, staff transferred test operations from Saltmarsh to the Bank's backup site in Amberford. The exercise used simulated payment instructions and did not move customer funds.

All 14 participating institutions connected successfully to the backup service. Processing resumed after 43 minutes, within the Bank's internal recovery limit of 60 minutes. The test included the loss of a primary communications link and a check that completed instructions could not be processed twice.

Observers identified two areas for improvement: clearer contact arrangements during staff changes and faster confirmation that every participant had received the recovery message. Neither affected the completion of the exercise. The Bank has assigned corrective actions and will track them through its operational risk programme. Normal settlement services remained available throughout.

```python
import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser

class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status):
        self.status = status
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}")

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")
    
    table = soup.find("table", class_="bok-table")
    if not table:
        return []
    
    tbody = table.find("tbody")
    rows = tbody.find_all("tr") if tbody else []
    
    records = []
    for row in rows:
        tds = row.find_all("td")
        if len(tds) < 2:
            continue
        
        date_el = tds[0]
        title_el = tds[1]
        
        date_text = date_el.get_text(strip=True)
        try:
            pub_date = parser.parse(date_text).date()
        except Exception:
            continue
        
        title_a = title_el.find("a")
        if not title_a:
            continue
        rel_url = title_a.get("href")
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except FetchError:
            continue
        
        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        page_head = release_soup.find(class_="page-head")
        h1 = page_head.find("h1") if page_head else release_soup.find("h1")
        title_text = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ""
        
        author = None
        # Look for author in meta or author tag; sample has none
        # Simple heuristic: find meta with name="author" or author meta
        meta_author = release_soup.find("meta", {"name": "author"})
        if meta_author and meta_author.get("content"):
            author = meta_author["content"].strip()
        # Also look for <span class="author"> etc. Not present; keep None
        
        rte = release_soup.find(class_="rte")
        body_parts = []
        if rte:
            paras = rte.find_all("p")
            for p in paras:
                text = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                if text.strip():
                    body_parts.append(text.strip())
        body = "\n\n".join(body_parts)
        
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title_text,
            "date": pub_date.isoformat(),
            "author": author,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere in the module's namespace
# from some_module import FetchError  # Not needed here as per instructions

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str):
    """
    Extract all press release records from the Meridian Ratings press listing.
    
    Args:
        fetch: Callable that performs HTTP GET and returns response body as str.
                Raises FetchError for HTTP errors.
        listing_url: URL of the press listing page (e.g., "/press/").
    
    Returns:
        List[Dict] with keys: url, title, date, author, body. Newest first.
    """
    # Fetch listing page
    try:
        listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    except Exception:
        return []

    # Check for RSS feed
    feed_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url.rstrip('/'), '/press/feed.xml')
    try:
        feed_html = fetch(feed_url)
        # Parse as XML
        feed_soup = BeautifulSoup(feed_html, "html.parser")
        channel = feed_soup.find("channel") or feed_soup.find("rss")
        if channel:
            items = channel.find_all("item")
            records = []
            for item in items:
                link_tag = item.find("link")
                title_tag = item.find("title")
                pub_date_tag = item.find("pubDate")
                desc_tag = item.find("description") or item.find("content")
                # Author may be in author tag or dc:creator
                author_tag = item.find("author")
                dc_creator_tag = item.find("dc:creator")
                # Get link
                if link_tag and link_tag.string:
                    link = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url.rstrip('/'), link_tag.string)
                else:
                    continue
                # Title
                title = title_tag.string.strip() if title_tag and title_tag.string else ""
                # Date
                date = None
                if pub_date_tag and pub_date_tag.string:
                    try:
                        pub_date = parser.parse(pub_date_tag.string)
                        date = pub_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                # Author
                author = None
                if dc_creator_tag and dc_creator_tag.string:
                    raw = dc_creator_tag.string.strip()
                    # Remove "By " prefix if present (unlikely in dc:creator)
                    if raw.lower().startswith("by "):
                        raw = raw[3:].strip()
                    author = raw
                elif author_tag and author_tag.string:
                    raw = author_tag.string.strip()
                    if raw.lower().startswith("by "):
                        raw = raw[3:].strip()
                    author = raw
                # Body: use description if available, else fetch release page
                body = ""
                if desc_tag and (desc_tag.string or desc_tag.get_text()):
                    desc_text = desc_tag.get_text(separator="\n\n", strip=True)
                    body = desc_text.strip()
                # If body empty or insufficient, fetch release page
                if not body or body.strip() == "":
                    try:
                        release_html = fetch(link)
                        rel_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
                        article = rel_soup.find("article", class_="pr")
                        if article:
                            # Remove meta and disclaimer
                            for meta in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "pr-meta" in x):
                                meta.decompose()
                            for disc in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "disclaimer" in x):
                                disc.decompose()
                            body_div = article.find("div", class_="pr-body")
                            if body_div:
                                paragraphs = body_div.find_all("p")
                                parts = []
                                for p in paragraphs:
                                    pt = p.get_text(strip=True)
                                    if pt:
                                        parts.append(pt)
                                body = "\n\n".join(parts)
                            else:
                                body = article.get_text(separator="\n\n", strip=True)
                        body = body.strip()
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                # Normalize author: keep as is, ensure no leading/trailing spaces
                if author:
                    author = author.strip()
                # Only include if date not None and body non-empty
                if date and body:
                    records.append({
                        "url": link,
                        "title": title,
                        "date": date,
                        "author": author if author else None,
                        "body": body
                    })
            # Sort by date descending
            records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
            return records
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Fallback to HTML parsing if feed not usable
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    # Look for press releases via pagination or direct links
    press_root = soup.find(id="press-root")
    if not press_root:
        press_root = soup.body

    release_links = []
    for link_tag in press_root.find_all("a", href=True):
        href = link_tag['href']
        full_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url.rstrip('/'), href)
        if full_url.startswith("/press/"):
            # Accept any /press/ link
            release_links.append(full_url)

    # Deduplicate
    seen = set()
    unique_links = []
    for link in release_links:
        if link not in seen:
            seen.add(link)
            unique_links.append(link)

    # Sort by date from URL descending
    def extract_date_from_link(link):
        path = link.split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
        parts = path.split('/')
        if len(parts) < 4:
            return None
        year_str, month_str, day_str = parts[1], parts[2], parts[3]
        try:
            year = int(year_str)
            month = int(month_str)
            day = int(day_str)
            return f"{year:04d}-{month:02d}-{day:02d}"
        except ValueError:
            return None

    dated_links = []
    for link in unique_links:
        date_str = extract_date_from_link(link)
        if date_str:
            dated_links.append((date_str, link))

    dated_links.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
    sorted_links = [link for _, link in dated_links]

    records = []
    for link in sorted_links:
        try:
            release_html = fetch(link)
        except Exception:
            continue

        rel_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        article = rel_soup.find("article", class_="pr")
        if not article:
            continue

        h1 = article.find("h1")
        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ""

        meta_div = article.find("div", class_="pr-meta")
        date_raw = None
        if meta_div:
            date_span = meta_div.find("span")
            if date_span:
                date_text = date_span.get_text(strip=True)
                try:
                    parsed = parser.parse(date_text)
                    date_raw = parsed.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
                except Exception:
                    pass

        if not date_raw:
            path = link.split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
            parts = path.split('/')
            if len(parts) >= 4:
                year = parts[1]
                month = parts[2]
                day = parts[3]
                try:
                    date_raw = f"{int(year):04d}-{int(month):02d}-{int(day):02d}"
                except ValueError:
                    pass

        author_span = article.find("span", class_="analyst")
        author_raw = None
        if author_span:
            text = author_span.get_text(strip=True)
            if text.lower().startswith("written by "):
                author_raw = text[12:].strip()
            else:
                author_raw = text

        body_div = article.find("div", class_="pr-body")
        body_text_parts = []
        if body_div:
            paragraphs = body_div.find_all("p")
            for p in paragraphs:
                pt = p.get_text(strip=True)
                if pt:
                    body_text_parts.append(pt)
            body = "\n\n".join(body_text_parts)
        else:
            # fallback
            for meta in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "pr-meta" in x):
                meta.decompose()
            for disc in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "disclaimer" in x):
                disc.decompose()
            body = article.get_text(separator="\n\n", strip=True)
        body = body.strip()

        if date_raw and body:
            author = author_raw if author_raw else None
            records.append({
                "url": link,
                "title": title,
                "date": date_raw,
                "author": author,
                "body": body
            })

    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
import re
from urllib.parse import urljoin
from datetime import datetime
from dateutil import parser as date_parser
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    """
    Extract all news releases from the listing page.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fetch : callable
        fetch(url) -> str (HTML). Raises FetchError on HTTP errors.
    listing_url : str
        Absolute URL of the listing page (e.g., "https://www.devvalbrume.example/nouvelles/").

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict]
        Each dict has keys: url, title, date, author, body.
        Newest first.
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup_listing = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")

    article_items = soup_listing.find_all("article", class_="nouvelle")
    records = []

    for item in article_items:
        h2 = item.find("h2")
        if not h2:
            continue
        link_tag = h2.find("a", href=True)
        if not link_tag:
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)

        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except Exception:
            # Skip if fetch fails
            continue
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")

        h1 = soup_release.find("h1")
        if h1:
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            title = ""

        date_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="date")
        if not date_tag:
            continue
        date_text = date_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        match = re.search(r"Publié\s+le\s+(\d+(?:er)?)\s+(\w+)\s+(\d{4})", date_text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        if not match:
            continue
        day_str = match.group(1)
        month_str = match.group(2).lower()
        year_str = match.group(3)
        day_num = int(re.sub(r"e?r$", "", day_str))
        month_map = {
            "janvier": 1, "février": 2, "mars": 3, "avril": 4, "mai": 5, "juin": 6,
            "juillet": 7, "août": 8, "septembre": 9, "octobre": 10, "novembre": 11, "décembre": 12
        }
        month_num = month_map.get(month_str)
        if month_num is None:
            continue
        try:
            day_clean = str(day_num)
            date_str = f"{day_clean} {month_str} {year_str}"
            dt = date_parser.parse(date_str, fuzzy=True)
            date_iso = dt.date().isoformat()
        except Exception:
            continue

        author_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="auteur")
        if author_tag:
            author_text = author_tag.get_text(strip=True)
            if author_text.lower().startswith("par "):
                author_text = author_text[4:].strip()
            author_text = author_text.rstrip(".")
            author_text = " ".join(author_text.split())
            author = author_text if author_text else None
        else:
            author = None

        contenu_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="contenu")
        if contenu_div:
            paras = []
            for p in contenu_div.find_all("p"):
                paras.append(p.get_text(strip=False).replace("\n", " ").strip())
            body = "\n\n".join(paras)
        else:
            body = ""

        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_iso,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)

    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
        pub_date = None

            if date_span:

        if author_span:

            # Remove trailing punctuation like commas
            author_part = author_part.rstrip(",.")
            author = author_part
            # If multiple authors? Not present; keep as is

        date_str = None
        if pub_date:
            date_str = pub_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        elif listing_dt:
            date_str = listing_dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        
        # Extract body from <section class="content__body">
        body_section = release_soup.find("section", class_="content__body")
        body_text_parts = []

                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                # Keep empty paragraphs? No, only non-empty

                    body_text_parts.append(txt.strip())
            body = "\n\n".join(body_text_parts)

                body_text_parts = [p.get_text(strip=True) for p in paras if p.get_text(strip=True)]
                body = "\n\n".join(body_text_parts)
            else:
                body = ""
        
        # Build record (only if date present)
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_str,  # may be None if no date found
            "author": author,
            "body": body
        }
        if record["date"]:
            records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by pub_date from release page (most reliable)
    def get_date(rec):
        d = rec["date"]
        if d and isinstance(d, str):
            try:
                return parser.parse(d).date()
            except Exception:
                return date.min
        return date.min
    
    records.sort(key=get_date, reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
        Each dict has keys: url, title, date, author, body.
        Newest first.
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup_listing = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")

    article_items = soup_listing.find_all("article", class_="nouvelle")
    records = []

    for item in article_items:
        h2 = item.find("h2")
        if not h2:
            continue
        link_tag = h2.find("a", href=True)
        if not link_tag:
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)

        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except Exception:
            # Skip if fetch fails
            continue
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")

        h1 = soup_release.find("h1")
        if h1:
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            title = ""

        date_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="date")
        if not date_tag:
            continue
        date_text = date_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        # Extract the part after "Publié le "
        match = re.search(r"Publié\s+le\s+(.+)", date_text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if not match:
            continue
        date_part = match.group(1)
        try:
            # dateutil can parse "8 octobre 2026", "6 octobre 2026", "17 septembre 2026", "1er septembre 2026"
            dt = date_parser.parse(date_part, fuzzy=True)
            date_iso = dt.date().isoformat()
        except Exception:
            continue

        author_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="auteur")
        if author_tag:
            author_text = author_tag.get_text(strip=True)
            # Remove leading "Par " (case insensitive) and any trailing punctuation
            if author_text.lower().startswith("par "):
                author_text = author_text[4:].strip()
            author_text = author_text.rstrip(".")
            # Keep only words (no job titles etc.; simple cleaning)
            words = author_text.split()
            # Remove common "Par" prefix already handled; keep all words
            # Join with " and " if multiple names? The site uses single author names like "Bastien Corvelin".
            # If there are multiple names separated by commas or "et", we join with " and ".
            # Simple approach: keep as is, but ensure no "Par " prefix.
            author = " ".join(words) if words else None
        else:
            author = None

        contenu_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="contenu")
        if contenu_div:
            paras = []
            for p in contenu_div.find_all("p"):
                # Get text without extra newline conversion; keep paragraph separation
                paras.append(p.get_text(strip=False))
            # Join paragraphs with a blank line; ensure no extra spaces at start/end of paragraphs
            body_lines = [p.get_text(strip=False).rstrip() for p in paras]
            # Remove empty paragraphs that may arise from tags
            body_lines = [line for line in body_lines if line.strip() != ""]
            body = "\n\n".join(body_lines)
        else:
            body = ""

        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_iso,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)

    # Sort by date descending (newest first)
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
```

```python
            # fallback: find #article and get its children excluding header/footer
            article_div = article_soup.find(id='article')
            if article_div:
                # get all text with blank lines between paragraphs
                paragraphs = []
                for child in article_div.find_all(['p', 'div', 'h2', 'h3'], recursive=False):
                    if child.get_text(strip=False).strip():
                        paragraphs.append(child.get_text(separator='\n', strip=False))
                body = '\n\n'.join(p.strip() for p in paragraphs if p.strip())
            else:

        else:
            # get text with blank lines between paragraphs
            body_text = body_elem.get_text(separator='\n\n', strip=False)
            # remove possible "Loading…" placeholder
            if 'Loading' in body_text:
                body = ""
            else:
                body = body_text.strip()
        
        # Build record
        record = {
            'url': abs_url,
            'title': title if title else '',
            'date': date_str if date_str else '',
            'author': author if author else None,

        }

    # Sort newest first: date descending
    def get_date(rec):
        d = rec['date']
        if not d:
            return datetime.min
        try:
            return parser.parse(d)
        except Exception:
            return datetime.min
    
    records.sort(key=get_date, reverse=True)
    return records
```
