Council approves revenue amendments following public September meeting

Last modified 28 September 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria approved amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 8, Revenue from Customer Contracts, at its public meeting on 16 September. All seven members present voted in favour, subject to final drafting checks.

Clearer treatment of contract changes

The amendments clarify when a change to agreed goods and prices forms a separate contract. They also explain when a company must update revenue already recognised. The Council considered 27 consultation responses and retained the proposed accounting approach.

  • Additional examples for staged deliveries
  • Clearer allocation of revised prices
  • Transition relief for completed contracts

Publication is planned for 6 October. The approved effective date is annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with early application permitted once the amendments are issued. The published text will set out the transition method and required disclosures. Companies should continue using the current published standard until the amendments are available.

Page reviewed
23 October 2026
First published
19 October 2026
Author
Lucien Marcelet
Reference
KSC-2026-857

The Kestria Securities Commission has asked six bond issuers to correct French disclosure documents following a review in Val-Brume. Staff examined 28 documents made available to investors in the French-speaking region and compared key payment terms with the corresponding English versions.

Four documents omitted wording about an issuer's right to repay bonds early. Two others gave an incorrect deadline for bondholders to submit payment instructions. The affected issues have a combined face value of KRN 96 million. The review did not identify any payment already missed because of these errors.

The six issuers must publish corrected documents and notify affected holders by 30 October. The Commission has also requested evidence of checks by staff with suitable language and financial knowledge. Issuers remain responsible for the accuracy of documents prepared by outside translators. Investors who believe a discrepancy has affected a payment should contact the issuer and may also report the matter to the Commission.

23 October 2026
First published
21 October 2026
Author
Dorian Pellac
Reference
KSC-2026-864

The securities court in Saltmarsh today ordered Ordelune Storage and two former executives to preserve records relevant to the Kestria Securities Commission's investigation into suspected false revenue statements. The order follows the Commission's application announced on 13 October and takes effect immediately.

The order covers accounting entries, customer contracts, invoices and related correspondence concerning KRN 18.6 million in reported storage service revenue. Those subject to it must suspend routine deletion of relevant electronic material and retain paper records. They must provide written confirmation of the preservation steps taken within seven days.

The court has not decided whether the revenue statements were false or whether any person breached securities law. The Commission's investigation continues, and the company and former executives retain the right to respond to any allegations. Preserving the records will allow the evidence to be examined. The Commission will announce any further public proceedings when they are filed.

Amberford bond issuer ordered to correct missing debt disclosures

Published
25 August 2026
Author
Dorian Pellac
Reference
KSC-2026-801

The Kestria Securities Commission has directed Amberford Heatworks to correct its latest half-year report after the bond issuer omitted information about a loan condition. The condition allows a lender to demand repayment if the company's cash reserves fall below KRN 6 million.

The company reported cash reserves of KRN 7.4 million at 30 June but did not explain the condition or the consequences of breaching it. The Commission considers this information necessary for investors assessing the company's ability to meet payments on its KRN 42 million bond issue.

Amberford Heatworks must publish a corrected report by 8 September and explain the changes in a separate market notice. The direction does not require early repayment of the bonds. No financial penalty has been imposed. The Commission will review the corrected report and consider whether further action is needed. Bond issuers remain responsible for explaining significant borrowing conditions in plain language.

September meeting papers cover revenue and reporting priorities

Last modified 9 September 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published papers for its public meeting in Saltmarsh on 16 September. The meeting will consider proposed clarifications to Kestrian Accounting Standard 8, Revenue from Customer Contracts, and priorities for the next reporting cycle.

Items for discussion

Staff have analysed 27 responses to the revenue consultation, which closed on 31 July. Respondents generally supported clearer treatment of contract changes, although several requested more detail on allocating revised prices to goods already delivered.

  • Revenue consultation findings
  • Examples involving revised contract prices
  • Research on smaller company disclosures
  • Progress against the annual work plan

The papers recommend amendments for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, but no decision has been made. Public observers may reserve one of 30 seats by 14 September. A written decision summary will be published after the meeting, including any changes to the staff recommendations.

Supplier finance consultation enters its final response period

Last modified 27 September 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria is reminding companies and users of accounts that comments on its supplier finance proposals close on 30 September. As at 18 September, the Council had received 16 written responses.

Evidence still sought

Early responses identify practical questions about obtaining information from finance providers. The Council is seeking further evidence on the time and cost involved, particularly where a company uses several providers or has arrangements covering suppliers in different parts of Kestria.

  • Availability of opening balance information
  • Time needed to change reporting systems
  • Usefulness of payment date ranges
  • Costs of gathering comparative figures

Responses may address individual questions rather than the whole draft. A company in Kestrel Bay, for example, could explain the records available for one arrangement without identifying its suppliers. The proposals remain subject to change. The suggested effective date is still 1 January 2028, and existing requirements continue to apply.

Council seeks views on clearer supplier finance disclosures

Last modified 19 August 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published proposed amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 14, Cash Flows and Financing. The proposals would require companies to explain arrangements under which a finance provider pays suppliers and the company later pays that provider.

Information proposed

The draft would introduce a single note showing the size and main terms of these arrangements. Companies would retain responsibility for deciding how the related liabilities and cash flows are classified under existing requirements.

  • Opening and closing liability balances
  • Amounts already paid to suppliers
  • Ranges of payment due dates
  • Significant changes without cash movements

Comments are invited by 30 September 2026. The Council particularly welcomes examples from manufacturers and wholesalers in Amberford and Ostara. Its initial proposal is for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028, with early application permitted. The final requirements and transition arrangements will depend on the evidence received.

Revenue amendments issued with relief for completed contracts

Last modified 6 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has issued amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 8, Revenue from Customer Contracts. They clarify the accounting for changes to promised goods and agreed prices, including changes made during a series of deliveries.

Effective date and transition

The amendments apply to annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027. Early application is permitted and must be disclosed. Companies must apply the changes to contracts that remain incomplete at the start of the first reporting period in which they use the amendments.

  • No reassessment of completed contracts
  • No restatement of comparative figures
  • Opening adjustment to retained earnings
  • Explanation of material transition effects

A new example follows an Ostara equipment maker whose customer adds KRN 180,000 of goods to an existing order. It explains how to assess the additional goods and their price. The issued package includes the amended wording, three worked examples and the Council's reasons for its decisions.

Council corrects illustrative lease example without changing requirements

Last modified 5 September 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has corrected a numerical error in the illustrative examples accompanying Kestrian Accounting Standard 11, Leases. The correction affects Example 6 in the supporting booklet published in June 2026.

Corrected payment total

The example describes equipment leased by a fictional workshop in Amberford. Four annual payments of KRN 24,000 were correctly shown in the payment schedule, but the accompanying sentence gave their total as KRN 94,000. That sentence now states KRN 96,000.

  • Payment schedule remains unchanged
  • Discounted calculations remain unchanged
  • Explanatory sentence has been corrected

The revised booklet is labelled September 2026 and includes a correction note beside the example. This is an editorial correction to supporting material, so it has no effective date or transition provisions. Companies do not need to change their accounting policies because of it. Printed copies distributed at Council workshops will include the corrected page.

Autumn workshop programme opens for company accounts teams

Last modified 27 August 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has opened registration for four autumn workshops on applying existing accounting requirements. Each session will offer 45 places, with attendance free of charge.

Practical sessions across Kestria

The programme covers Saltmarsh on 10 September, Kestrel Bay on 17 September, Ostara on 24 September and Val-Brume on 1 October. The Val-Brume session will be delivered in French, with the same worked examples and supporting material as the other sessions.

  • Recognising revenue from staged deliveries
  • Estimating provisions for repairs
  • Presenting material accounting policies
  • Recording questions for Council staff

Participants may submit questions when registering. Staff will use those questions to select examples, including transactions valued between KRN 20,000 and KRN 500,000. The workshops explain current standards and do not create additional requirements. Places will be allocated in order of registration, initially limited to two people from each company or practice.

Workshop report identifies recurring questions from accounts preparers

Last modified 7 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published a report on its four autumn workshops. A total of 163 people attended sessions in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara and Val-Brume between 10 September and 1 October.

Questions informing future support

Participants submitted 58 questions before the sessions and raised further examples during discussion. Staff grouped the questions by topic, with revenue recognition and repair provisions accounting for just over half of the advance submissions.

  • Evidence supporting repair estimates
  • Revenue from partly completed deliveries
  • Choosing useful accounting policy information
  • Explaining changes in estimates

The report summarises recurring difficulties and includes six examples drawn from the sessions, with company details replaced by invented facts. It explains the standards in force during the workshops. The revenue amendments issued on 6 October are available separately. Staff will use the findings when proposing next year's educational programme; the report itself introduces no accounting requirements.

French editions of October amendments now available together

Last modified 16 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published French editions of the revenue amendments issued on 6 October and the supplier finance amendments issued on 15 October. Both are available without charge through the Council's publications service.

Consistent wording and examples

Language staff in Val-Brume reviewed the editions alongside technical staff to keep defined terms consistent with the existing French standards. Each package contains the amendments, transition provisions and the same worked examples as its English counterpart.

  • Revenue amendments to Standard 8
  • Supplier finance amendments to Standard 14
  • Updated accounting terms glossary
  • Matching paragraph references throughout

Publication in French does not alter either effective date. The revenue amendments apply to annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, and the supplier finance amendments from 1 January 2028. Early application is permitted under each package. Readers may report suspected translation errors by quoting the standard number, paragraph reference and wording concerned.

Ostara Homes Outlook Turns Negative as Sales Slow and Debt Rises

29 September 2026 | Written by Tomas Belwick

Meridian Ratings has revised the outlook on Ostara Homes to negative from stable and affirmed its BBB minus long-term issuer rating. Slower reservations and higher spending on land have increased borrowing. The company builds mid-priced homes in Ostara, Amberford and the outer districts of Saltmarsh.

Net reservations fell 14% in the eight months to August compared with the same period last year. Completed but unsold homes increased to 246 from 171 at December. Net debt reached KRN 392 million, equivalent to 3.7 times operating profit before depreciation over the preceding 12 months.

Cash and undrawn committed facilities total KRN 168 million, against KRN 61 million of debt due within a year. This supports the rating despite weaker trading. Meridian could lower the rating if inventory continues to build or net debt remains above four times operating profit before depreciation for a sustained period.

Meridian Rates Saltmarsh Waterworks Bond in Line With Issuer Rating

10 September 2026 | Written by Mara Ternell

Meridian Ratings has assigned an A minus rating to Saltmarsh Waterworks’ proposed KRN 180 million senior unsecured bond. The issue rating matches the company’s long-term issuer rating, which remains A minus with a stable outlook. The bond is expected to mature in September 2033.

The company intends to use KRN 120 million of the proceeds to repay a bank loan due in February 2027. The balance will fund pipe replacement and treatment equipment within its existing investment programme. The transaction would extend debt maturities while leaving total borrowing within Meridian’s previous forecasts.

The proposed bonds will rank equally with the company’s other senior unsecured obligations. Meridian’s assessment assumes that the final terms are consistent with the draft documents reviewed. Cost overruns or a material increase in borrowing beyond the current programme could weaken financial headroom, but neither is included in the base forecast.

Council publishes supplier finance feedback ahead of decision

Last modified 13 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published a summary of responses to its proposed supplier finance disclosures. The consultation closed on 30 September with 34 responses from companies, lenders, accounts users and accounting practices.

Support and implementation concerns

Twenty-six respondents supported a single note bringing together information about these arrangements. Several companies said that opening balances and comparative figures would be costly to obtain for the first year, especially where finance providers hold part of the information.

  • Broad support for closing balances
  • Requests for clearer scope wording
  • Concerns about comparative information
  • Support for a 2028 effective date

The Council will consider the proposals at its public meeting in Saltmarsh on 14 October. Staff recommend retaining the proposed annual effective date and adding first-year relief for opening balances and comparatives. These are recommendations only. The Council has not yet approved final amendments, and companies should continue applying the existing standard.

New supplier finance disclosures include first year transition relief

Last modified 15 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has issued amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 14, Cash Flows and Financing, following approval at its meeting on 14 October. The amendments require a note explaining supplier finance arrangements and their effect on company liabilities.

Requirements from 2028

The amendments apply to annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028, with early application permitted and disclosed. The note must describe key terms, opening and closing liabilities, amounts already paid to suppliers, payment date ranges and significant changes without cash movements.

  • Comparatives waived in the first year
  • Opening balances waived in the first year
  • Closing balances required from initial application
  • Existing classification requirements retained

The Council added transition relief after considering 34 consultation responses. For a calendar-year company first applying the amendments in 2028, the initial note will therefore include its closing position at 31 December 2028 without corresponding 2027 figures. The publication includes a scope example involving an Amberford wholesaler.

Meridian Ratings Affirms Saltmarsh Waterworks at A Minus With Stable Outlook

17 August 2026 | Written by Mara Ternell

Meridian Ratings has affirmed Saltmarsh Waterworks’ long-term issuer rating at A minus with a stable outlook. The rating reflects steady demand, predictable regulated income and adequate funding for repairs. The company supplies drinking water to 284,000 households and businesses in and around Kestria’s capital.

Revenue reached KRN 418 million in the year to June, up 4.8% from the previous year. Cash generated from operations covered interest payments 5.2 times. Water lost through leaks fell to 18.6% from 20.1%, although older pipes in the eastern districts remain a significant maintenance cost.

The stable outlook assumes annual capital spending of about KRN 110 million and no substantial debt-funded expansion. Available cash and committed borrowing facilities cover debt falling due over the next 18 months. A sustained increase in debt without matching earnings growth could put pressure on the rating.

Research invitation focuses on smaller company reporting costs

Last modified 19 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria is inviting smaller companies to join a research study on the cost of preparing annual accounts. The study will inform its work plan and does not propose changes to any standard.

Thirty companies sought

Staff aim to recruit 30 companies with annual revenue between KRN 2 million and KRN 40 million. The sample will cover manufacturing, retail and services, with participants sought in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume.

  • Hours spent gathering supporting records
  • Costs of external accounting advice
  • Disclosures requiring substantial judgement
  • Information used by lenders and owners

Expressions of interest close on 13 November 2026. Selected participants will be asked to complete one questionnaire and attend a 60-minute interview in English or French. Findings will be published in grouped form, without naming participating companies. The Council will assess the evidence before deciding whether any reporting topic needs further research or public consultation.

Meridian Assigns BBB Rating to Amberford Packaging With Stable Outlook

25 August 2026 | Written by Tomas Belwick

Meridian Ratings has assigned Amberford Packaging a first-time long-term issuer rating of BBB with a stable outlook. The company produces paper-based food containers and industrial wrapping at two plants in Amberford. Its established customer relationships support earnings, although exposure to pulp prices limits the rating.

Amberford Packaging reported revenue of KRN 762 million and operating profit before depreciation of KRN 126 million for the year to June. Its five largest customers accounted for 38% of sales. Contracts covering roughly two-thirds of revenue allow material cost increases to be passed through within three months.

The company plans to spend KRN 74 million on a replacement production line over the next year. Meridian expects net debt to remain below 2.8 times operating profit before depreciation. The stable outlook assumes the project stays within budget and customer demand remains broadly consistent with current orders.

Kestrian Food Producers Maintain Stable Outlook as Input Costs Ease

9 October 2026 | Written by Céline Arvane

Meridian Ratings has maintained a stable outlook for Kestria’s packaged food sector. Lower grain and container costs are helping producers rebuild margins, although household spending remains subdued. Across six rated companies, average operating margins increased to 11.2% in the first half of 2026 from 10.4% a year earlier.

Sales volumes rose just 0.8%, with stronger demand for basic products offset by weaker purchases of premium lines. Producers supplying retailers in Saltmarsh and Amberford reported increased use of promotions. Meridian expects price competition to limit how much of the recent cost relief companies retain.

The sector’s median net debt stood at 2.4 times operating profit before depreciation at June. Most rated producers have sufficient cash and committed facilities for planned investment over the next year. Debt-funded acquisitions or prolonged discounting would create greater pressure than the modest volume growth currently assumed in Meridian’s forecasts.

Meridian Upgrades Kestrel Bay Savings After Stronger Capital and Lower Arrears

3 September 2026 | Written by Elian Voss

Meridian Ratings has upgraded Kestrel Bay Savings’ long-term issuer rating to A minus from BBB plus. The outlook is stable. The upgrade reflects a sustained improvement in capital and loan quality, supported by retained earnings and a reduction in lending to speculative property developments.

The bank’s core capital ratio reached 15.4% at the end of June, compared with 13.6% a year earlier. Loans more than 90 days overdue declined to 1.2% of gross lending from 2.0%. Customer deposits funded 86% of loans, limiting reliance on borrowing from financial markets.

These improvements give the bank greater capacity to withstand the margin pressure affecting Kestrian regional lenders. Meridian nevertheless expects earnings growth to slow as savings rates rise. The stable outlook assumes that management maintains its current lending standards and does not materially increase distributions to shareholders.

Kestrian Regional Banks Face Narrower Margins Despite Steady Loan Demand

24 August 2026 | Written by Elian Voss

Meridian Ratings expects profitability at Kestria’s regional banks to weaken modestly during the remainder of 2026 as deposit costs rise. Its review of eight rated lenders found that average net interest margins fell to 2.7% in June from 2.9% in December. The sector outlook remains stable.

Loans grew by 3.6% over the same period, led by small business borrowing in Ostara and residential lending around Saltmarsh. Customer deposits increased by 2.8%. Banks have offered higher rates on fixed-term accounts to retain savers, reducing the benefit of growth in interest income.

Arrears remain manageable, with loans more than 90 days overdue representing 1.8% of the reviewed portfolios. Construction borrowers account for much of the recent increase. Meridian expects lenders to maintain current capital buffers, but banks with concentrated property exposure have less room to absorb unexpected losses.

Meridian Places Bracken Freight Under Review Following Proposed Harbour Acquisition

8 October 2026 | Written by Tomas Belwick

Meridian Ratings has placed Bracken Freight’s BBB long-term issuer rating under review for downgrade after the company announced an agreement to acquire Kestrel Bay Harbour Services. The proposed KRN 460 million purchase would expand Bracken’s storage and cargo handling operations but could materially increase debt.

Bracken has disclosed a committed bridge loan covering the full purchase price. It is also considering an equity issue, although the amount and timing have not been confirmed. Based on debt-only funding, Meridian estimates that net debt could exceed four times annual operating profit before depreciation immediately after completion.

The review will examine the final funding mix, integration costs and the acquired business’s cash generation. Bracken expects completion before the end of October, subject to the remaining transaction conditions. Meridian will resolve the review once it has sufficient evidence to assess the combined company’s financial position.

Val-Brume Heating Retains BBB Plus Rating Ahead of Winter Demand

5 October 2026 | Written by Céline Arvane

Meridian Ratings has affirmed Val-Brume Heating’s BBB plus long-term issuer rating with a stable outlook. The company provides district heating to 42,000 properties in Kestria’s French-speaking region. Its established network and contracted customer base support the rating, while seasonal cash needs and fuel costs remain constraints.

Fuel stocks at the end of September covered approximately 11 weeks of expected winter consumption. Fixed-price supply contracts cover 76% of forecast purchases through March 2027. The company also has an undrawn KRN 65 million revolving facility available to meet short-term working capital requirements.

Meridian expects operating cash flow to cover interest payments at least four times over the coming year. The forecast allows for routine maintenance and a KRN 28 million boiler replacement. An unusually prolonged cold period would increase purchases, but existing liquidity provides a reasonable buffer against that pressure.

Meridian Publishes Updated Criteria for Rating Kestrian District Heating Providers

12 October 2026 | Written by Mara Ternell

Meridian Ratings has published updated criteria for assessing district heating providers in Kestria. The criteria take effect today and apply to new ratings and future reviews. They give more detailed guidance on fuel procurement, seasonal liquidity and the financial effect of delays in recovering costs through customer tariffs.

The update follows a consultation that closed on 18 September. Meridian received nine written responses from rated companies, investors and other market participants. The final text clarifies how analysts assess committed credit facilities and distinguishes fuel already held in storage from purchases covered by future supply contracts.

Meridian has assessed its existing district heating ratings against the revised criteria and identified no immediate rating changes. The update does not alter the rating or outlook on Val-Brume Heating affirmed on 5 October. Individual reviews will continue to consider network condition, customer concentration and each provider’s ability to absorb unexpected costs.

Meridian Downgrades Ostara Homes as Cancellations Increase and Liquidity Weakens

23 October 2026 | Written by Céline Arvane

Meridian Ratings has downgraded Ostara Homes’ long-term issuer rating to BB plus from BBB minus. The outlook is negative. The downgrade follows a sharp increase in cancellations and a reduction in available borrowing facilities, which weaken the company’s ability to carry its growing stock of unsold homes.

Figures supplied on 21 October show that completed but unsold homes reached 289 at September, compared with 246 at August. Cancellations accounted for 27% of gross reservations during September. Cash and undrawn committed facilities fell to KRN 112 million after a lender declined to renew a KRN 40 million facility.

Ostara Homes has suspended new land purchases and plans selective discounts to release cash from finished properties. These steps should help liquidity, but lower selling prices will put further pressure on earnings. Meridian could lower the rating again if available funding falls materially or sales fail to cover construction spending and scheduled debt payments.

Amberford Water Receives A- Rating for Network Renewal Bond

By Mara Vellin and Céline Maret
September 18, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has assigned an A- rating to Amberford Water's proposed KRN 230 million senior unsecured bond, with a stable outlook. The company plans to use KRN 150 million to repay existing debt and the remainder to replace ageing mains and pumping equipment. The rating is subject to final documents matching the terms reviewed.

Amberford Water supplies 340,000 households and businesses under a licence that links permitted revenue to operating costs and approved investment. Collections remained strong at 98.6% of billed revenue in the year ended June. Water losses declined to 17.2% from 19.1% following repairs to several older sections of the network.

Northstar expects debt to remain close to 4.0 times annual operating profit before depreciation during the renewal programme. The stable outlook assumes spending stays within the approved budget and service performance supports timely cost recovery. Persistent overspending or debt above 4.8 times operating profit could put downward pressure on the rating.

Meridian Affirms Fenmere Commercial Bank as Property Lending Remains Concentrated

19 October 2026 | Written by Elian Voss

Meridian Ratings has affirmed Fenmere Commercial Bank’s BBB long-term issuer rating with a stable outlook. The Saltmarsh-based lender benefits from steady business deposits and adequate capital. Its relatively large exposure to commercial property continues to constrain the rating, particularly lending secured on smaller office buildings.

Commercial property represented 31% of gross loans at the end of September, down from 34% a year earlier. Loans more than 90 days overdue rose to 2.5% from 2.1% over that period. Additional provisions reduced nine-month profit to KRN 47 million, 12% below the comparable period.

The bank’s core capital ratio of 14.2% provides capacity to absorb further losses within Meridian’s base forecast. Deposits increased by 3.1% during the first nine months, supporting liquidity. The stable outlook assumes gradual reductions in property concentration and no sharp deterioration among the bank’s largest borrowers.

Northstar Opens Consultation on Proposed Corporate Liquidity Assessment Changes

By Nalin Verdan and Dario Selven
September 10, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has opened a consultation on proposed changes to its corporate liquidity methodology. The draft explains how analysts would assess seasonal cash needs, restrictions on moving cash between subsidiaries and borrowing facilities that depend on financial conditions. Written responses are invited until 2 October.

The proposal would require a separate assessment of the weakest three-month cash position within the following year. Current analysis places greater emphasis on the full twelve-month period. The draft also clarifies that an uncommitted overdraft would not count as an assured funding source, even when an issuer has used it regularly.

An initial review of 24 rated Kestrian corporate groups suggests that five could receive weaker liquidity assessments under the draft. This would not automatically change their ratings, which also reflect business strength and debt levels. The existing methodology remains in force during consultation. Northstar will publish its conclusions after reviewing responses and completing further testing.

Northstar Credit Analytics has lowered Val-Brume Packaging's senior unsecured bond rating to BB+ from BBB-. The outlook is stable. The producer of cartons and food containers has reported weaker earnings and a larger working capital requirement than Northstar assumed in its previous review.

Kestrian Food Producers Face Narrower Margins as Packaging Costs Rise

By Elise Dorne and Nalin Verdan
August 20, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has revised its outlook for Kestrian packaged food producers to negative from stable. The change reflects higher packaging and distribution costs, together with limited scope to raise selling prices. It is a sector assessment and does not change any individual bond rating.

Across the agency's sample of seven fictional issuers, packaging costs increased by an average of 11% in the first half of 2026, while selling prices rose 3%. Northstar expects the sample's operating margin before depreciation to fall to roughly 9% this year from 10.4% in 2025. Smaller producers supplying shops around Ostara have less purchasing power and face the greatest pressure.

Most rated producers retain adequate cash reserves and have no large bond repayments within twelve months. This should limit immediate rating pressure. The agency will focus on stock levels, customer payment times and whether cost savings protect cash generation. Companies that borrow to fund dividends while margins weaken could face individual rating reviews.

Northstar Credit Analytics has affirmed Estuary Freight's BBB- senior unsecured bond rating and revised the outlook to negative from stable. The Kestrel Bay cargo handler has KRN 160 million of bonds falling due in February 2027. Discussions with lenders are continuing, but the company has not secured replacement funding.

At 31 July, Estuary Freight held KRN 38 million in unrestricted cash and had KRN 25 million available under committed facilities. Cargo volumes fell 6% in the first seven months of the year, mainly because of lower building material shipments. Northstar estimates debt at 4.4 times annual operating profit before depreciation, against 3.8 times at the end of 2025.

The negative outlook reflects the narrowing time available to refinance. Northstar could lower the rating if funding arrangements remain incomplete or operating performance weakens further. Ostara Rental Housing Outlook Remains Stable Despite Higher Maintenance Spending

By Mara Vellin and Dario Selven
October 8, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained a stable sector outlook for rated rental housing companies operating in Ostara. High occupancy and steady rent collection continue to support earnings, although repairs and borrowing costs are absorbing more cash. The assessment covers four issuers with a combined 28,400 homes.

Average occupancy stood at 97.4% at the end of August, compared with 97.1% a year earlier. Rent arrears remained modest at 1.8% of annual billed rent. Maintenance spending rose 8%, led by roof repairs and heating replacements. Fixed interest rates apply to 76% of the sample's debt, limiting the immediate effect of higher financing costs.

Northstar expects most issuers to fund routine repairs from rental income while keeping development programmes within committed borrowing limits. Ratings could come under pressure where large construction projects coincide with debt maturities. The stable sector outlook assumes occupancy remains above 96% and companies retain enough accessible funding to meet twelve months of planned spending.

Northstar Adopts Revised Liquidity Methodology with Seasonal Cash Guidance

By Nalin Verdan and Céline Maret
October 14, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has published its revised corporate liquidity methodology, effective today. The final document adds a review of the weakest three-month cash position within the following year and clarifies how analysts treat restricted cash, uncommitted borrowing and conditions attached to committed facilities.

Following consultation, the agency has added worked examples for seasonal businesses. Analysts may recognise expected customer receipts when supported by a consistent collection record, but must also test a reasonable delay. Cash held by a subsidiary will count only where it can legally and practically meet the obligations being assessed.

Northstar has also published an anonymised summary of the twelve consultation responses. It will apply the revised methodology to existing corporate ratings over the next three months and to new assignments immediately. Publication itself changes no ratings. Any resulting action will receive a separate release explaining the issuer's circumstances and the role of the revised assessment.

Corporate Liquidity Consultation Closes with Twelve Responses Under Review

By Nalin Verdan and Céline Maret
October 5, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics received twelve responses to its proposed corporate liquidity methodology changes before the consultation closed on 2 October. Submissions came from rated companies, bond investors and lending firms. Analysts are reviewing the comments alongside additional testing of the proposed three-month cash assessment.

Several respondents supported clearer treatment of restricted cash and uncommitted borrowing. Others asked how the agency would assess seasonal businesses whose lowest cash balance occurs shortly before a predictable collection period. Four submissions requested worked examples showing how financial conditions attached to borrowing facilities would affect available liquidity.

Northstar will consider these points before deciding whether to adopt the changes. No rating or liquidity assessment has changed as a result of the consultation, and the existing methodology remains applicable. The agency plans to publish a summary of the main comments with its final decision. Confidential financial information supplied by respondents will be excluded from that summary.

Estuary Freight Downgraded to BB as Refinancing Options Narrow

By Tomas Arven and Dario Selven
October 15, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has lowered Estuary Freight's senior unsecured bond rating to BB from BBB- and concluded the review opened on 13 October. The outlook is negative. Further information supplied during the review shows that the company has limited readily available funding for its KRN 160 million February 2027 bond repayment.

Of the KRN 25 million previously reported as available under committed facilities, KRN 15 million expires in January 2027. Northstar therefore excludes that amount when assessing resources for the bond maturity. The proposed storage yard sale remains at an early stage, with no agreed buyer or binding timetable. September cargo earnings also fell below management's revised budget.

The downgrade principally reflects weaker refinancing prospects and reduced financial flexibility. The revised liquidity methodology published yesterday also informs the assessment of facility availability. The negative outlook indicates further downside if replacement funding remains unsecured. A stable outlook would require a credible, committed repayment plan and enough cash to continue ordinary operations.

Kestrian Retail Bond Issuers Enter Winter with Uneven Cash Buffers

By Elise Dorne and Nalin Verdan
October 20, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained a negative outlook for Kestrian discretionary retailers in its latest sector review. Households are limiting larger purchases, while retailers have already paid for much of their winter stock. The agency expects differences in cash reserves to matter more than modest changes in reported sales.

Among six rated issuers, stock values at the end of September were 9% higher than a year earlier, while sales for the preceding three months rose only 1%. Two chains operating mainly in Saltmarsh and Kestrel Bay increased promotional discounts to clear older goods. Across the sample, average operating margins before depreciation fell to 6.2% from 7.1%.

Four issuers have committed facilities extending beyond their seasonal borrowing peak. The remaining two rely more heavily on cash generated during winter trading. Northstar is testing slower stock sales and delayed supplier credit separately for each company. The sector outlook does not imply that every retailer will be downgraded, and no individual rating changes accompany this report.

Bracken Grid Bond Rating Holds After Amberford Storm Disruption

By Tomas Arven and Mara Vellin
October 9, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained Bracken Grid's BBB senior unsecured bond rating and stable outlook following the 6 October storm in the Amberford district. The storm damaged overhead lines and interrupted supplies to 74,000 connections. By the evening of 8 October, the company had restored power to all but 1,900 affected connections.

Bracken Grid's preliminary estimate places repair costs at KRN 18 million to KRN 24 million. Northstar has assumed the full upper estimate in its initial assessment without relying on insurance receipts. The company had KRN 72 million in cash and KRN 110 million of undrawn committed facilities at the end of September.

These resources should allow repairs to proceed without materially weakening liquidity. The rating also allows for occasional weather-related disruption. Northstar will review the final repair bill, compensation payments and any changes to planned maintenance. Costs substantially above the current estimate, or evidence of wider network weaknesses, could alter the assessment.

Val-Brume Packaging Rating Affirmed After Investment Spending Is Reduced

By Céline Maret and Dario Selven
October 22, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has affirmed Val-Brume Packaging's BB+ senior unsecured bond rating and stable outlook after the company reduced its investment budget. Management has deferred a second printing line, cutting planned spending for the current financial year to KRN 18 million from KRN 34 million.

The decision preserves cash while the company addresses the working capital pressures behind its September downgrade. Unrestricted cash stood at KRN 22 million at the end of September, with KRN 35 million still available under its committed facility. Early collections from overdue customers helped the improvement, although one month of stronger receipts does not establish a sustained recovery.

Northstar continues to expect debt near 5.0 times annual operating profit before depreciation in the near term. The revised liquidity assessment supports the existing rating because available resources cover projected seasonal needs. An upgrade would require durable earnings recovery and lower debt. Renewed cash outflows, weaker facility access or substantial additional borrowing could lead to another downgrade.

Equipment programme expands after strong demand from regional manufacturers

Devran Holt · 28 September 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank has increased its equipment lending programme from KRN 40 million to KRN 60 million. Since applications opened on 24 August, the bank has approved KRN 26.4 million across 19 facilities. Of that amount, KRN 11.8 million has been drawn by borrowers.

Companies in Amberford and Ostara account for just over half the approved lending by value. Purchases include cutting machines, temperature-controlled storage and packing lines. Approval totals represent agreed facilities rather than equipment already installed, and borrowers draw funds as supplier invoices become due.

The additional allocation is available to new applications from today. Loan sizes remain between KRN 250,000 and KRN 4 million, with terms of three to seven years. Each application will receive a separate credit assessment. Businesses should obtain approval before relying on bank funding to place a binding equipment order.

Devran Holt · 24 August 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank today opened a KRN 40 million lending programme for mid-sized companies replacing production equipment. Businesses across Kestria can apply for loans of between KRN 250,000 and KRN 4 million, with repayment terms of three to seven years.

Bank publishes revised fees for business lending administration

Leonie Venn · 2 September 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank has published a revised schedule of business lending administration fees, taking effect on 5 October. The fee for a borrower-requested security amendment will fall from KRN 450 to KRN 325. Providing a duplicate annual interest certificate will become free, replacing the current KRN 35 charge.

The fee for reviewing a request to extend an overdraft temporarily will rise from KRN 175 to KRN 225. It covers the review and does not guarantee approval. Customers will be told whether a charge applies before they ask the bank to proceed with any chargeable work.

The changes do not alter agreed loan margins or repayment dates. Where an existing agreement fixes an administration fee, that agreement will continue to apply. The full schedule is available from relationship teams and on the bank’s website, with copies in French available for customers in Val-Brume.

Val-Brume lending desk adds appointments for French-speaking businesses

Tomas Arlen · 3 September 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank has added twelve weekly appointments at its Val-Brume lending desk for businesses that prefer to discuss borrowing in French. The additional sessions are available on Tuesdays and Thursdays and can be held at the branch or by telephone.

Appointments cover working capital, equipment purchases and reviews of existing facilities. Businesses can request a document checklist in French before their meeting. The desk will also help customers identify which financial records are needed, although it cannot prepare accounts or provide independent legal advice.

There is no appointment charge and no obligation to apply for a loan. Lending decisions remain subject to the bank’s usual affordability and security checks. The expansion follows a six-week booking review in which the Val-Brume team recorded an average wait of nine working days for a French-language lending appointment.

Business reference rate falls by a further quarter point

Mara Ellery · 18 September 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank will lower its business reference rate from 6.25% to 6.00% on 21 September. Borrowers whose agreements track this rate will receive the reduction automatically. The change follows the quarter-point reduction that took effect on 24 August.

Together, the two changes reduce annual interest by KRN 5,000 on an unchanged KRN 1 million balance, before any fees and subject to the terms of the agreement. Fixed-rate borrowing is unaffected. Loans linked to a different reference rate will continue to follow the calculation set out in their contracts.

The bank reviewed its funding costs and lending commitments before making the decision. Updated repayment information will be sent where monthly payments change. Customers with interest-only facilities will see the new rate applied to the relevant days in their next interest calculation and can request a breakdown from their relationship team.

New borrower support team offers earlier repayment difficulty reviews

Devran Holt · 22 October 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank has established a dedicated borrower support team for business customers facing repayment difficulties. The five-person team is based in Saltmarsh and accepts referrals from relationship managers across Kestria. Customers can also ask their usual lending contact for a support review.

Ostara businesses offered working capital review appointments this month

Tomas Arlen · 6 October 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank is offering 30 working capital review appointments for mid-sized businesses at its Ostara branch between 12 and 30 October. The sessions are intended for companies preparing for seasonal changes in stock purchases, customer payments or supplier bills.

Coppermere Components Upgraded to BBB After Sustained Debt Reduction

By Elise Dorne and Mara Vellin
October 19, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has raised Coppermere Components' senior unsecured bond rating to BBB from BBB-, with a stable outlook. The Amberford manufacturer supplies replacement parts for industrial pumps and ventilation equipment. The upgrade reflects sustained debt reduction, a broader customer base and improved cash collection.

Debt fell to KRN 126 million at the end of August from KRN 171 million eighteen months earlier. Over the same period, debt relative to annual operating profit before depreciation declined from 3.8 times to 2.6 times. The largest customer now accounts for 14% of revenue, compared with 23% two years ago. Replacement orders provide more consistent demand than sales tied to new construction.

Cash and committed facilities comfortably cover the company's lowest projected three-month funding position under Northstar's revised methodology. The stable outlook assumes moderate investment and no large debt-funded acquisition. A downgrade could follow if debt rises above 3.5 times operating profit for a sustained period or customer concentration increases materially.

Harrow & Finch Bank lowers its business reference rate

Mara Ellery · 18 August 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank will reduce its business reference rate from 6.50% to 6.25% on 24 August. The change applies to lending agreements that track the bank’s reference rate. Fixed-rate loans will keep their agreed rates until the end of their fixed terms.

A company with a KRN 2 million loan priced at the reference rate plus 2 percentage points would pay around KRN 417 less interest over a full month, assuming its balance stays unchanged. Actual savings will depend on the number of days in the interest period and the outstanding balance.

The bank is sending notices to affected borrowers this week. Customers do not need to submit a request to receive the reduction. Relationship teams in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume can explain how the change will appear on individual statements.

Harrow & Finch Bank has introduced a revised monthly statement layout for variable-rate business loans. Statements issued from today show the reference rate, the borrower’s agreed margin and the number of days charged at each rate in a single interest table.

Where a rate changes during the statement period, separate rows show the balance and calculation for each part of that period. This will help borrowers check interest following the bank’s reference rate reductions in August and September. Fees will continue to appear separately from interest.

Council publishes spending update and revises research timetable

Last modified 22 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published its operating update for the nine months ended 30 September 2026. Expenditure totalled KRN 3.42 million against a phased budget of KRN 3.60 million.

Resources and delivery

The KRN 180,000 difference mainly reflects vacant research posts and lower venue costs. Technical staffing stood at 18 filled posts out of 20 at the period end. The update also records progress on consultations, educational material and public access to Council meetings.

  • Revenue amendments issued in October
  • Supplier finance amendments issued in October
  • Smaller company research recruitment opened
  • Intangible assets research timetable revised

The Council now expects to publish its preliminary intangible assets research paper in February 2027, two months later than previously planned. Staff time has been reassigned to complete the current amendments and support their introduction. The timetable change does not alter any accounting requirement or effective date. The full-year operating budget remains KRN 4.80 million.

Half-year results show lending growth and higher impairment charges

Mara Ellery · 21 October 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank today reported profit before tax of KRN 18.6 million for the six months ended 30 September 2026, compared with KRN 17.9 million a year earlier. Operating income rose to KRN 52.4 million from KRN 48.7 million, while operating costs increased to KRN 27.1 million from KRN 25.6 million.

The charge for expected lending losses increased to KRN 6.7 million from KRN 5.2 million. The increase mainly reflected weaker repayment prospects among a small number of wholesale borrowers. Gross customer lending reached KRN 1.24 billion at the period end, up from KRN 1.17 billion on 31 March 2026.

New lending drawn during the half year totalled KRN 186 million. Customer deposits stood at KRN 1.41 billion on 30 September. The bank continued to fund equipment purchases and working capital across Kestria while reviewing borrowers showing early signs of payment difficulty. The results are unaudited.

GreenBasket Supermarkets opened its Eastmere store in Amberford today, bringing its network to 215 shops across Kestria. The 1,420-square-metre store employs 46 people, including 31 colleagues recruited locally. It has eight staffed checkouts, a bakery and a collection desk for online orders.

GreenBasket recalls selected oat biscuits after incorrect allergen labelling

9 September 2026Sofia Merrow, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets is recalling its 250-gram Honeyfield Oat Biscuits with batch code HB0902 and a best-before date of 18 February 2027. The affected packs contain milk, which is missing from the allergen statement. They are unsuitable for people with a milk allergy.

The biscuits were sold in 87 GreenBasket stores across Kestria between 3 and 8 September. Customers with a milk allergy should not eat them. Anyone who bought an affected pack can return it to any GreenBasket store for a full refund without a receipt. Other batch codes are not included in this recall.

GreenBasket identified the error during a packaging check yesterday and removed the affected stock from sale that evening. Recall notices are displayed in the relevant stores and on the customer website. Product safety manager Orla Venn said the company had received no reports of illness linked to the affected batch.

New Val-Brume supermarket brings GreenBasket network to 216 stores

21 September 2026Mara Fenwick, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets opened its 216th store today in the Montelier district of Val-Brume. The KRN 8.6 million investment has created 62 jobs. The store has 2,100 square metres of sales space and includes a bakery, fresh fish counter and covered collection bays for online orders.

Signs, customer information and checkout instructions are available in French, reflecting the language used across the region. Store manager Lucien Varel said all customer-facing teams included French-speaking colleagues. The opening range includes cheese, preserves and baked goods from 29 regional producers, with supplier names displayed beside the products.

The building occupies a former storage yard that had stood empty for six years. GreenBasket retained the site's boundary trees and installed a rainwater tank for cleaning outdoor areas. A pedestrian entrance connects directly with the Montelier footpath, while bicycle stands and customer parking are located on opposite sides of the building.

Half-year sales rise as GreenBasket reports lower operating profit

30 September 2026Daniel Rooke, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets, Kestria's largest supermarket chain by store count, reported revenue of KRN 6.42 billion for the 26 weeks ended 30 August 2026, up 4.1 per cent on the comparable period. Sales at stores open for at least a year rose 2.7 per cent.

Operating profit fell from KRN 206 million to KRN 193 million. Higher wage and refrigeration maintenance costs outweighed savings in distribution. GreenBasket invested KRN 118 million in stores, equipment and delivery vehicles during the period, including the Eastmere opening in Amberford. It ended the half year with 215 stores.

Finance director Anika Pell said customers were buying more own-label groceries and making smaller, more frequent trips. Own-label products accounted for 58 per cent of grocery units sold, compared with 55 per cent a year earlier. Online orders represented 9.4 per cent of revenue, up from 8.7 per cent in the comparable period.

GreenBasket publishes clearer rules for supplier deductions and invoice disputes

15 October 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has introduced a supplier code covering invoice disputes, delivery deductions and changes to orders. Effective today, the code requires buyers to provide written reasons and supporting records before making a deduction. It applies to all goods suppliers across the company's 216 stores.

Suppliers now have a single route for challenging deductions through a commercial review team separate from their usual buyer. The code sets a ten-working-day deadline for an initial written response. Undisputed invoice amounts remain payable under the supplier's agreed terms while a challenge is examined.

Procurement director Nella Corven said discussions with 73 suppliers had highlighted inconsistent explanations for shortages and damaged deliveries. The new code also requires written agreement before suppliers are charged for a promotion. It does not change the 14-day payment terms for eligible small businesses, whose first payment report was published yesterday.

Small suppliers receive shorter payment terms under new purchasing policy

26 August 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has introduced payment terms of 14 calendar days for qualifying small suppliers, replacing its previous standard of 30 days. The policy applies to new purchase orders issued from today. A total of 186 existing suppliers meet the published eligibility rules.

Suppliers qualify if their annual turnover is below KRN 12 million and they employ fewer than 50 people. Payment is measured from receipt of a valid invoice after delivery. GreenBasket has removed the administration charge previously applied when suppliers requested payment before their contractual due date.

Procurement director Nella Corven said smaller producers often paid wages and bought materials well before receiving money for their goods. A dedicated accounts team in Saltmarsh now handles questions about the scheme. Suppliers can check eligibility and invoice status through their existing account, or request the same information by telephone.

Ostara depot changes cut damaged produce deliveries by nearly a quarter

8 October 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has reduced damaged fruit and vegetable deliveries from its Ostara depot by 24 per cent following changes to packing and loading. The result compares damage recorded per thousand crates during July to September with the same three months of 2025.

The depot supplies 68 stores and handles about 410,000 produce crates each month. Changes included shallower crates for soft fruit, separate loading positions for heavier root vegetables and temperature checks at each loading bay. GreenBasket spent KRN 1.7 million on equipment and training for the work.

Depot manager Brenna Holt said staff had recorded where damage occurred before changing handling routines. The measured reduction represents approximately 7,800 fewer damaged crates over the quarter. Produce rejected by stores remains subject to the same quality checks, and items suitable for sale are assessed separately from stock that must be discarded.

Kestrel Bay branch sets temporary hours during roof repairs

28 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail will shorten opening hours at its Kestrel Bay Harbour Lane branch while contractors replace part of the roof. From 5 to 16 October, the store will open from 9 am to 6 pm each day. Its usual opening hours are 7 am to 9 pm.

A routine building inspection found worn seals above the homeware stockroom. The affected storage area has been cleared, and work will take place behind a separate barrier. The repair budget is KRN 640,000. Grocery shopping, the pharmacy counter and customer toilets will remain available during the temporary opening hours.

Online collection customers with bookings outside the revised hours will be contacted directly and offered another slot or free home delivery. Staff will retain their contracted pay, with some shifts moved to stock preparation and nearby delivery operations. Lumen expects normal hours to resume on 17 October, subject to the final building inspection.

8 September 2026Mara Fenwick, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has completed a KRN 3.8 million refurbishment of its Harbour Steps store in Kestrel Bay. The shop remained open throughout the eight-week project. Work included replacement refrigeration, clearer aisle signs and a redesigned entrance with more space around baskets and trolleys.

The store now offers quieter shopping sessions on Tuesday and Thursday mornings between nine and ten. Lumen will provide weekly order forecasts and pay agreed invoices within 21 days. Both businesses will review unsold quantities each month, with the aim of reducing surplus without leaving shelves empty late in the day. Existing bakery suppliers will continue serving Lumen stores outside the expanded delivery area.

First payment report shows progress for GreenBasket small suppliers

14 October 2026Daniel Rooke, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has published its first payment report since introducing 14-day terms for qualifying small suppliers on 26 August. Of the 2,460 invoices due under the scheme by 30 September, 96.2 per cent were paid within the agreed period. Average payment time was 12.6 calendar days.

The report covers invoices with a combined value of KRN 18.4 million. Ninety-four were paid late, most following internal approval delays. All 94 had been settled by 9 October. GreenBasket has added a daily review of approaching payment deadlines and assigned a named contact to each participating supplier.

Finance director Anika Pell said the late payments fell short of the company's commitment. The report lists disputed invoices separately and does not count them as paid on time. Seventeen invoices remained in dispute at the reporting date, with reasons supplied to the businesses concerned. The figures cover the small-supplier scheme rather than GreenBasket's entire supplier base.

Lumen Home Retail has agreed a two-year vegetable supply programme with Reedplain Growers, a group of 18 farms outside Amberford. The programme covers potatoes, carrots, onions and cabbages sold in Lumen stores across Kestria. The first deliveries under the new terms begin on 1 October.

Val-Brume stores introduce clearer French labels across household essentials

Lumen Home Retail has introduced clearer French-language shelf labels at its three Val-Brume stores. The change covers 2,300 household and grocery products, including cleaning supplies, bedding and cupboard staples. Product names, pack sizes and unit prices now appear together in a larger, consistent format.

Lumen agrees new credit facility to support planned store investment

23 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail has signed a KRN 120 million revolving credit facility with Brackenmere Commercial Bank and Ternfold Lending. The facility matures in September 2030 and replaces a KRN 90 million agreement that was due to expire next year. It provides funds that Lumen can draw and repay as needed.

At signing, KRN 28 million was drawn under the new agreement to repay the outstanding balance on the previous facility. The remaining capacity is available for seasonal stock purchases and planned investment in stores and distribution equipment. No shares were issued as part of the financing.

Finance director Sella Morven said the agreement gave Lumen greater certainty over funding while retaining room for quieter trading periods. Interest is charged at a variable reference rate plus an agreed margin. The facility includes quarterly borrowing and interest-cover tests. Lumen met those requirements at signing and has not changed its full-year investment budget of KRN 34 million.

Lumen outlines Saltmarsh depot upgrade ahead of winter trading

Words by Elira Venn

23 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail will invest KRN 4.6 million in new sorting equipment and additional chilled holding space at its Saltmarsh distribution depot. Installation is scheduled to begin on 2 November and finish in stages by mid-December. The project forms part of the retailer's existing KRN 34 million annual investment budget.

The upgrade will add 320 chilled pallet spaces and replace two ageing conveyor sections used for household goods. Lumen expects the changes to reduce manual handling and give stores more flexibility when ordering fresh food. The depot currently supplies 27 of the company's 42 stores, including branches in Ostara and Val-Brume.

Work will take place in separate sections while normal deliveries continue. Lumen has leased temporary chilled storage for the installation period and scheduled staff training before each new section enters use. Eight maintenance and warehouse roles are being recruited. The company expects to assess delivery accuracy and equipment reliability after the upgraded sections have operated for eight weeks.

Lumen kept prices unchanged on its 150-item Everyday Basket throughout the quarter. Higher delivery costs were partly offset by fuller vehicle loads and lower food waste. Ostara tray plant cuts trim waste through tooling changes

By Tobin Merrow · September 29, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging's Ostara plant has reduced trim waste on two chilled-food tray lines following changes to cutting tools and sheet positioning. Across eight weeks of measured production, trim represented 13.1 per cent of material fed into the lines, down from 16.4 per cent during the preceding eight weeks.

Corvel is reporting the reduction as a material efficiency measure; it has not calculated a carbon saving from the work.

Corvel Packaging adds carton capacity at Amberford plant

By Mara Venn · August 25, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has brought a second carton folding line into service at its Amberford plant. The line adds capacity for 1.8 million food cartons a month, increasing the site's monthly folding capacity to 7.2 million units. It handles sleeves and folding cartons used for chilled meals, bakery products and dry foods.

Installation and production trials cost KRN 4.6 million. During acceptance checks, staff ran six carton sizes and measured fold accuracy, glue application and print alignment. Kestrel Bay store resumes full hours after completed roof repairs

Words by Tobin Rusk

21 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail's Harbour Lane store in Kestrel Bay resumed its usual 7 am to 9 pm opening hours on 17 October, following completion of roof repairs. The final inspection was completed on 16 October, allowing the homeware stockroom to return to use before the store reopened the following morning.

The work replaced worn roof seals and a damaged section of insulation above the stockroom. The final cost was KRN 618,000, compared with the KRN 640,000 budget. Contractors completed the repairs within the planned period, and the grocery section remained open throughout the temporary reduction in hours.

During the work, 286 collection bookings were moved to alternative times and 74 customers accepted free home delivery. Store manager Iven Rosk thanked customers for adjusting their visits and staff for covering revised shifts. The temporary collection arrangements have now ended, and the full homeware range is available on the shop floor again.

Corvel introduces separate energy surcharge on food packaging orders

By Ellis Dacre · August 31, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has introduced an energy surcharge of KRN 42 per tonne on cartons, trays and films dispatched from today. The charge applies to domestic orders across Kestria and appears as a separate invoice line. Base product prices are unchanged.

The surcharge reflects higher electricity and process heating costs at the company's Amberford, Ostara and Kestrel Bay plants. Corvel's combined energy cost per tonne of finished packaging was 14 per cent higher in August than in May, despite lower consumption on several production lines.

For an order weighing 2.5 tonnes, the surcharge is KRN 105 before tax. It does not apply to goods dispatched before today, even where the invoice is issued later. Customer statements show the dispatch weight used in the calculation, and account teams have received a common worksheet to explain the charge and resolve weight queries.

Corvel publishes evidence sheets for selected carton recycling claims

By Tobin Merrow · October 9, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has issued evidence sheets for 18 uncoated carton specifications supplied from Amberford. Each sheet identifies the board grade, coatings, inks and adhesives covered by the assessment. It also explains the conditions attached to the company's recycling statements.

The sheets draw on fibre separation tests and checks of collection guidance available in Saltmarsh, Amberford and Val-Brume. Results apply only to the listed specifications. Cartons with film windows, barrier layers or heavy food contamination require separate consideration and are outside the scope of this release.

Customers can request a sheet using their carton specification number. The documents support packaging decisions but do not establish that every local collection service accepts a carton. Corvel advises customers to check disposal wording against the collection arrangements serving their buyers. No new recycling claim has been added to customer artwork as part of this work.

Corvel opens French language customer desk in Val-Brume

By Nadia Pell · October 5, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has opened a French language customer desk in Val-Brume to support food producers in Kestria's French-speaking region. Three customer service staff now handle order enquiries, delivery updates and invoice questions from the office. The desk operates on weekdays from 08:30 to 17:00 local time.

Customers can request quotations, specification summaries and surcharge explanations in French. Technical approval remains with the production site responsible for the packaging. The desk uses the same order records as Corvel's Saltmarsh team, allowing staff to check quantities and dispatch information without creating a separate customer account.

The office supports customers buying cartons, trays and films; it does not hold stock or receive returned goods. During its internal service trial, staff handled 64 sample enquiries covering all three product groups. Customers already assigned an account manager retain that contact and can use the new desk for routine order support.

Harvest Review Trims Wheat Estimate As Oat Outlook Holds

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 28, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has revised its member wheat harvest estimate to 179,500 tonnes, down from the August estimate of 184,000 tonnes. The oat estimate is now 52,400 tonnes, compared with 52,000 tonnes previously. The review uses completed field records and updated reports received by 27 September.

Lower wheat yields around Ostara account for most of the reduction. Amberford results remain close to the earlier estimate. Members report that 81 per cent of their wheat area and 69 per cent of their oat area has been harvested, leaving uncertainty around the remaining fields.

The co-operative has accepted 96,800 tonnes of wheat and 21,600 tonnes of oats into its stores. These intake figures exclude grain still held on farms and must not be added to the harvest estimate. By Ellis Dacre · October 20, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has reduced its energy surcharge from KRN 58 to KRN 31 per tonne for goods dispatched from today. The lower rate applies to cartons, trays and films across its production sites. It replaces the rate introduced on 22 September.

The reduction follows lower purchased electricity costs and reduced heating demand during the latest four-week review period. Energy costs remain above the May reference level used when Corvel introduced the surcharge. The company continues to calculate the charge separately from product base prices.

Bramble Foods agrees purchase of Val-Brume specialist bakery

By Mara Fenwick

18 September 2026

Bramble Foods has agreed to acquire Hearthmere Bakery, a privately owned producer of crispbreads and seeded biscuits based in Val-Brume, for KRN 24.6 million in cash. The purchase remains subject to competition clearance and customary completion conditions. Completion is expected by the end of October.

Hearthmere Bakery employs 86 people at a single production site in Kestria's French-speaking region. It recorded revenue of KRN 31.8 million in its last financial year. Its range would add specialist baked snacks to Bramble Foods' existing bakery and biscuit business.

Bramble Foods intends to retain the Hearthmere name, the Val-Brume site and its workforce. The proposed acquisition would be funded from existing cash and committed borrowing facilities. Until completion, both businesses will continue to operate independently. Bramble Foods has not included any contribution from Hearthmere in its current trading expectations and will provide a further announcement when the transaction completes.

Amberford Receiving Yard Introduces Separate Queues For Wheat And Oats

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Aug. 21, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has introduced separate wheat and oat queues at its Amberford receiving yard. The change follows a trial involving 38 deliveries, during which the average time from arrival to unloading fell from 54 minutes to 37 minutes. Both lanes use the existing weighbridge.

Drivers must identify their crop and booking reference at the entrance before joining a queue. Loads still require sampling, weighing and acceptance checks. A separate holding area is available for vehicles whose grain needs further testing, allowing other accepted loads to move through the yard.

The yard has received 2,640 tonnes of new-season grain so far, mostly wheat from farms south of Amberford. Members without a booking should contact the receiving office before travelling. The co-operative has also added clear signs at the approach road and pedestrian crossing beside the sampling room.

New Oat Quality Report Supports Food Processing Orders

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Oct. 12, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's latest oat quality report records an average test weight of 54.8 kilogrammes per hectolitre and average moisture of 12.9 per cent. The results cover 18,300 tonnes sampled across its Amberford, Ostara and Val-Brume stores. Each reported parcel has completed intake testing.

Screenings averaged 2.1 per cent by weight. Of the volume covered, 16,700 tonnes met the co-operative's standard food oat specification without further cleaning. Buyers can request parcel summaries showing moisture, test weight and screenings from the sales desk. Bramble Foods announces October price changes for selected snacks

By Tobin Vale

20 August 2026

Bramble Foods has notified retail customers of price increases averaging 2.5% across selected biscuits and savoury snacks, effective from 1 October 2026. The changes apply to wholesale list prices in Kestria. Standard sliced bread and plain bread rolls are excluded from this announcement.

The company said higher costs for edible oils, cocoa ingredients and flexible packaging had continued through the summer. Savings from purchasing and factory improvements have absorbed part of those increases. Individual product changes will vary, and retailers will decide the prices paid by shoppers.

Bramble Foods is giving customers six weeks to update ordering systems and review planned promotions. Existing promotional agreements covering September will be honoured. Customer teams based in Saltmarsh and Kestrel Bay will provide revised price lists and product details directly to retailers. Pack weights and recipes will remain unchanged as part of this price review.

New oat cracker range reaches Kestrian shops this month

By Tobin Vale

23 September 2026

Bramble Foods will begin supplying its new Bramble Table oat crackers to retailers on 28 September. The range comprises plain oat, toasted onion and garden herb varieties in 180 gram packs. Distribution will start in Saltmarsh and Ostara before extending to other parts of Kestria during October.

The crackers are made at the company's Ostara snacks plant using an existing baking line adapted during the summer. Bramble Foods has invested KRN 620,000 in mixing equipment and product development. The recommended retail price is KRN 2.80 per pack, although individual retailers will set their own selling prices.

Development included tasting sessions with 240 adult volunteers and checks on breakage during transport. The company has arranged an initial eight-week production programme, with later output dependent on repeat orders. Ingredient and allergen information will appear on every pack, alongside storage guidance intended to help customers keep opened crackers fresh.

Completed Harvest Returns Confirm Wheat And Oat Crop Totals

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Oct. 20, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Completed harvest returns from all 426 supplying farms put Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's member crop at 180,200 tonnes of wheat and 53,100 tonnes of oats. The totals replace the estimates issued in September. Wheat production was 5.8 per cent above last season, while oat production rose by 7.2 per cent.

The final wheat figure is 700 tonnes above the September estimate, with later Amberford fields contributing most of the difference. Oats finished 700 tonnes above the revised estimate. Members supplied harvested area and weighed production records, with separate estimates for the small amount of grain retained in unweighed farm bins.

Co-operative stores have received 158,600 tonnes of wheat and 44,800 tonnes of oats from this harvest. The balance remains on farms for later delivery, farm use or other sales. Production totals describe the member crop and do not represent the quantity available for immediate purchase from the co-operative.
