Bramble Foods reports higher first half sales and operating profit

By Mara Fenwick

17 August 2026

Bramble Foods, the listed Kestrian bakery and snacks company, today reported revenue of KRN 428.6 million for the six months ended 30 June 2026, up 6.4% on the same period last year. Operating profit rose to KRN 34.2 million from KRN 30.8 million. Sales volumes increased by 2.1%, with the remaining revenue growth coming from prices and changes in the mix of products sold.

Packaged bread performed steadily, while savoury crackers and small cake packs recorded stronger growth. Lower waste at the Amberford bakery helped offset higher flour and packaging costs. Net debt at the period end was KRN 76.5 million, compared with KRN 81.3 million a year earlier.

The board declared an interim dividend of KRN 0.12 per share, payable on 30 September to shareholders registered on 4 September. Bramble Foods continues to expect modest volume growth during the second half, although household spending remains uneven across Kestria.

Competition clearance received for proposed Hearthmere Bakery acquisition

By Mara Fenwick

9 October 2026

Bramble Foods has received clearance from Kestria's competition authority for its proposed acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery. The KRN 24.6 million cash transaction was announced on 18 September. Clearance satisfies one of the principal conditions of the purchase agreement, with completion still subject to the remaining customary requirements.

The companies are now preparing final completion documents and arrangements for transferring ownership. Bramble Foods continues to expect the transaction to complete by the end of October. Hearthmere remains independently owned and managed until that process has concluded.

Stock Check Confirms Grain Records Across Four Storage Sites

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Oct. 22, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has completed its autumn stock check at Amberford, Ostara, Kestrel Bay and Val-Brume. Measured stocks at the close of 21 October totalled 121,460 tonnes of wheat and 34,280 tonnes of oats. The figures include grain already allocated to customers but awaiting collection.

Staff compared bin measurements with receiving tickets, dispatch weights and recorded cleaning losses. The combined difference between measured grain and stock records was 0.08 per cent, within the co-operative's internal tolerance of 0.20 per cent. All four sites completed checks, and no unexplained difference required a customer allocation to be changed.

Routine temperature readings also found no storage parcel above the co-operative's action threshold of 20 degrees. Store teams continue to check grain condition and record aeration work. Customers requesting available volumes should contact the sales desk, as total physical stock includes committed grain and parcels held for further preparation.

About Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative
Prairie Gold is owned by 4,100 farming families and handles about a fifth of Kestria's wheat and oat harvest.

Media contact: Communications office, 061 2290 0000, media@prairiegold.example

October snack price changes take effect across customer orders

By Tobin Vale

5 October 2026

Bramble Foods has implemented the wholesale price changes announced on 20 August. Revised prices took effect on 1 October for selected biscuits and savoury snacks, with an average increase of 2.5% across the affected range. Standard sliced bread and plain bread rolls remain outside this review.

The company's customer service teams checked the first orders under the revised lists last week. A small number of invoice queries are being resolved directly with retailers. Deliveries have continued to schedule, and no product withdrawals or changes to pack weights have accompanied the price adjustment.

Bramble Foods said the increase addresses part of the higher ingredient and packaging costs reported during the summer. Retailers continue to set their own shelf prices and promotional offers. The company will monitor order patterns over the coming weeks, recognising that a few days of trading cannot establish how shoppers will respond to any resulting shelf price changes.

Bramble Foods has completed the initial commissioning trials for its new cake packing line at Amberford. Trial packs met the site's checks for seal strength, weight accuracy and product protection. Third quarter sales rise as bakery demand remains steady

By Mara Fenwick

19 October 2026

Bramble Foods recorded revenue of KRN 219.4 million for the three months ended 30 September 2026, an increase of 4.8% compared with the same quarter last year. Revenue for the first nine months reached KRN 648.0 million. Third-quarter sales volumes grew by 1.3%, supported by steady bread demand and higher cracker sales.

Trading remained strongest in Saltmarsh and Amberford, while orders from smaller shops were more variable. The new oat cracker range began shipping near the quarter end and made only a small contribution. Wholesale price changes introduced on 1 October had no effect on the reported quarter.

The board's full-year operating profit expectations remain unchanged. Regular production on Amberford's new packing line began today, with performance monitoring under way. The proposed Hearthmere Bakery acquisition has received competition clearance but has not yet completed. Its trading is therefore excluded from these figures, and completion remains expected by the end of October.

Kestrel Bay bakery completes oven heat recovery installation

By Leonie Varnet

20 October 2026

Bramble Foods has brought a new heat recovery system into service at its Kestrel Bay bakery following installation during planned maintenance. The KRN 1.3 million system captures heat from oven exhausts and uses it to warm water for cleaning. It serves two bread ovens at the site.

Engineering estimates suggest the equipment could reduce the bakery's annual purchased energy use by around 6%. Actual savings will depend on production hours and seasonal demand for hot water. Bramble Foods will compare meter readings with production volumes over the next six months before reporting a measured result.

Installation took place over three scheduled maintenance weekends, with bread deliveries maintained from existing stocks and production at other group bakeries. Maintenance staff have received training on cleaning and inspection requirements. The project forms part of the company's approved factory investment programme and does not change the site's production capacity or staffing levels.

Bramble Foods completes acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery in Val-Brume

By Mara Fenwick

21 October 2026

Bramble Foods today completed its acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery for KRN 24.6 million in cash. All remaining completion conditions have been satisfied following competition clearance announced on 9 October. Hearthmere's financial results will be included in Bramble Foods' group accounts from today.

The Val-Brume business makes crispbreads and seeded biscuits and employs 86 people. Its name, production site and workforce have been retained. Customers will continue to place orders through their existing contacts, and current supply agreements remain in effect. Product recipes and packaging are unchanged at completion.

The purchase was funded through a combination of available cash and drawings under Bramble Foods' existing borrowing facilities. During the first three months of ownership, work will concentrate on reporting systems, supplier arrangements and planning for future orders. Bramble Foods expects a small contribution to group revenue for the remainder of 2026 and will provide further detail with its full-year results.

Posted: Thursday, August 20, 2026
Posted by: Elin Veymar

Oakhill Bakeries Group has begun consultation with the 31 employees at its Ostara bakery over a proposal to close the site. No final decision has been made. The bakery produces sandwich rolls and plain buns in a building with limited space for modern equipment.

The site has a daily capacity of 14 tonnes, although average output over the past six months was eight tonnes. Maintenance and energy costs per tonne have risen as production has fallen. The company is examining whether work can be transferred to its other bakeries.

Employees have received written details of the proposal and can attend individual meetings during paid working time. Oakhill is considering alternatives submitted by staff, including changes to shifts and products. Managing director Tessa Oakhill said the consultation must allow employees to question the figures and put forward workable options.

Posted: Friday, October 16, 2026
Posted by: Mara Denholt

Oakhill Bakeries Group reduced bread production waste to 2.8 per cent of baked weight in September, down from 3.6 per cent in June. The comparison covers Amberford, Saltmarsh and Ostara, which operated during both months. It excludes the new Kestrel Bay bakery.

The measure includes misshapen loaves, products damaged during packing and bread rejected during quality checks. It does not include unsold goods returned by shops, which Oakhill records separately. Production waste across the three sites fell from 54 tonnes in June to 43 tonnes in September.

Teams adjusted dough portion settings, improved checks at shift changes and replaced worn guides on two packing lines. Operations director Brenna Halewick said these small changes reduced avoidable losses without relaxing product standards. Site teams review the figures weekly, using weighing records and production totals to identify where further checks are needed.

Industrial gas users in Ostara receive pressure advisory

Published: 22 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued a supply advisory for large gas users connected to the East Ostara industrial branch. A pressure regulator fault identified this morning has reduced the branch's available capacity from 92 to 76 megawatt hours per hour. Household gas connections are unaffected.

The network operator has contacted the 14 sites holding interruptible supply agreements on the branch. Under those agreements, affected sites must keep within the individual limits stated in their notices. The Board has confirmed that the combined reduction requested from these sites is 16 megawatt hours per hour.

Engineering staff are assessing the faulty equipment. No loss of gas containment has been reported. Other industrial customers should continue to follow their existing supply terms and should not change equipment settings on the basis of this advisory alone. News release

Gas network ruling disallows unsupported maintenance costs

Published: 30 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has disallowed KRN 1.8 million of maintenance costs claimed by the Saltmarsh gas network operator. The ruling follows a review of expenditure for the year ended 30 June. The operator did not provide sufficient work records to support costs assigned to 23 maintenance jobs.

The disputed amount forms part of a KRN 41.6 million maintenance claim. The Board accepted KRN 39.8 million after checking invoices, inspection records and staff time entries. The disallowed costs cannot be recovered through regulated network charges. This decision does not alter the tariff currently shown on customer bills.

The ruling concerns evidence supporting expenditure. It makes no finding that the maintenance itself was unnecessary or that the network is unsafe. The operator must keep clearer records linking each charge to completed work. A summary of the assessment explains the evidence requirements and lists the categories of costs that were excluded.

Board clarifies billing rules following household tariff reduction

Published: 17 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued billing guidance following the household electricity standing charge reduction on 15 September. The guidance addresses questions received from customers and suppliers about bills covering days on both sides of the change. It does not introduce another tariff change.

For a bill covering 1 to 30 September, suppliers must charge 14 days at KRN 0.84 and 16 days at KRN 0.79. The standing charge for that period is therefore KRN 24.40. Electricity used during the period remains subject to the unchanged unit rate of KRN 0.246 per kilowatt hour.

Customers using advance credit meters are also entitled to the lower standing charge from 15 September. Where a meter update has taken longer, suppliers must credit the difference. News release

Ostara industrial gas restrictions lifted after equipment repairs

Published: 29 September 2026

Supply restrictions on the East Ostara industrial gas branch have been lifted following repairs to a pressure regulator. The Kestria Energy Board confirmed the change after reviewing test records supplied by the network operator. The branch has returned to its normal available capacity of 92 megawatt hours per hour.

The restrictions affected 14 sites with interruptible supply agreements from 22 September. The operator recorded a total requested reduction of 16 megawatt hours per hour during the restriction period. It has reported no interruption to household supplies and no loss of gas containment associated with the equipment fault.

Affected businesses have received individual notices cancelling their temporary limits. The Board has requested maintenance records and an explanation of how the fault developed. This review is separate from the decision to restore capacity. Businesses disputing a charge connected with the restriction should first use their supplier's complaints process and retain their meter records.

Electricity tariff decision reduces standard household standing charge

Published: 15 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has approved a reduction in the standard household electricity standing charge from KRN 0.84 to KRN 0.79 a day. The decision applies from today to customers on the regulated standard tariff. The electricity unit rate remains KRN 0.246 per kilowatt hour.

The reduction reflects lower verified costs for billing and customer account administration. For a household remaining on the tariff for a full 365 days, the standing charge difference is KRN 18.25. News release

Board publishes annual review of electricity network charges

Published: 20 August 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has published its annual review of electricity network charges. The review covers the cost of carrying power to homes and businesses across Kestria. It records KRN 184 million in allowed network revenue for the year ended 30 June, against actual spending of KRN 179 million.

Most of the difference came from delayed cable replacement in Amberford and lower maintenance costs around Saltmarsh. The Board has required network operators to explain how the unspent allowance is recorded in their accounts. Operators cannot treat money allowed for unfinished work as an unrestricted surplus.

The review does not change customer tariffs. It also reports that average electricity interruptions fell from 74 minutes to 68 minutes per customer over the year. Rural districts west of Ostara remained above that average, at 112 minutes. The full review includes separate spending and service tables for each network area.

The Kestria Energy Board's Val-Brume office has introduced an additional weekly session for customers seeking help with electricity and gas bills. The service provides advice in French and English. It covers tariff explanations, estimated readings, disputed charges and the steps involved in making a formal complaint.

The additional session follows a rise in local enquiries from 86 in July to 129 in September. Most concerned estimated bills and difficulties obtaining account corrections. News release

Board approves lower overnight network charge for industry

Published: 16 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has approved a lower overnight electricity network charge for eligible industrial connections in Kestrel Bay. From today, the charge for electricity carried between midnight and 05:00 is KRN 0.018 per kilowatt hour, down from KRN 0.023. Other network rates remain unchanged.

The decision covers 38 connections with meters that record consumption in half-hour periods. Network evidence showed spare capacity during the overnight window and lower costs for carrying additional demand at those times. The Board accepted the proposed reduction after checking the operator's demand records and allocation of costs.

A qualifying site using 100,000 kilowatt hours entirely within the overnight window pays KRN 500 less in network charges for that consumption. This is only one part of its electricity bill. Energy supply prices, capacity charges and other applicable items are separate. Suppliers must identify the revised network rate clearly in their billing calculations.

News release

Meter checks find errors in industrial electricity bills

Published: 13 October 2026

A Kestria Energy Board audit has identified incorrect meter multipliers on nine industrial electricity accounts in Kestrel Bay. A multiplier converts the meter's recorded reading into the amount of electricity supplied. Using the wrong value can produce an incorrect bill even when the meter itself works properly.

Seven accounts were overcharged by a combined KRN 286,400 over periods ranging from four to eleven months. Two accounts were undercharged by a combined KRN 31,700. The supplier has accepted the findings and issued corrected account statements. All nine affected businesses have been contacted individually.

The Board has required repayment of the overcharges and a check of the supplier's remaining industrial meter settings. Any recovery of undercharges remains subject to the applicable billing rules and complaint rights. The audit found an account configuration problem, with no evidence of a fault in the physical meters or an interruption to electricity supply.

Quarterly report records fewer unresolved energy billing complaints

Published: 20 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has published its complaints report for July to September. It received 642 electricity and gas complaints during the quarter, compared with 689 in the preceding quarter. There were 118 unresolved cases at the end of September, down from 151 at the end of June.

Billing accounted for 61 per cent of new complaints. The most common issues were estimated consumption, delayed corrections and unclear account balances. Connection delays accounted for a further 17 per cent. The figures cover cases brought to the Board after customers had first raised the matter with their supplier or network operator.

News release

Amberford electricity connection delays prompt formal improvement notice

Published: 6 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued a formal improvement notice to the Amberford electricity network operator after an audit found repeated delays in providing connection quotations. Of 160 complete applications examined, 47 had not received a quotation within the required 15 working days.

The applications covered small shops, workshops and housing developments. The longest recorded wait was 38 working days. The operator attributed the backlog to vacancies and incomplete internal handovers. The Board found that these problems did not remove its obligation to meet the published service standard.

The notice requires weekly reporting of outstanding quotations and a named contact for every affected applicant. It also requires the operator to separate applications awaiting customer information from those delayed within its own teams. The notice imposes no financial penalty. Applicants can ask the operator for a written explanation of their case and use the Board's complaints route if it remains unresolved.

A 45-metre section of Berth Four returned to service today following the completion of concrete repairs and load testing on three replacement mooring bollards. The available working length is now 255 metres. The remaining 50 metres of the repair area are still fenced off.

Strong winds interrupt crane operations across container terminal

Ellis Corven 3 Sep 2026

Container crane operations at the Port of Kestrel Bay were suspended between 05:40 and 11:10 today after wind speeds exceeded the terminal's operating limit. Instruments on the quay recorded gusts of 78 kilometres per hour. Cranes were secured, and staff were withdrawn from exposed working areas.

Three vessels experienced delays, including one using the reduced working area at Berth Four. By 14:00, all operational cranes had returned to service following safety checks. Shipping agents have received revised departure estimates based on the remaining cargo moves for each vessel.

Freight gates remained open, but some drivers waited longer while container lifts were paused. The authority cancelled waiting charges for vehicles held inside the terminal during the suspension. No injuries, dropped containers or damage to lifting equipment were reported. Repair crews at Berth Four also stopped exposed work during the strongest winds.

Container volumes rise as inland rail services expand

Mara Venn 21 Aug 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay handled 84,600 standard container units in July, an increase of 6.2 per cent compared with July last year. Food products, household goods and machine parts accounted for most of the growth. The figures count a forty-foot container as two standard units.

Rail carried 28 per cent of containers leaving the port by land, up from 24 per cent a year earlier. Two additional weekly services between the port and Amberford began operating in June. The inland terminal at Amberford now receives eight port trains each week.

Average lorry turnaround time was 43 minutes during July, measured from entry at the freight gate to departure. This was four minutes shorter than in June. The authority publishes these figures to help hauliers and cargo owners compare port performance. Empty containers and loaded containers are included in the gate measure.

September figures show shorter queues at freight gates

Mara Venn 5 Oct 2026

Average lorry turnaround time at the Port of Kestrel Bay fell to 39 minutes in September, compared with 43 minutes in July. The monthly figure covers 31,480 completed visits and includes time spent waiting inside the terminal. Visits cancelled before arrival are excluded.

The port handled 82,900 standard container units during September. This was 2.4 per cent above the same month last year, despite the wind stoppage on 3 September and the reduced working length at Berth Four. Rail accounted for 29 per cent of containers leaving the port by land.

Gate staff recorded fewer arrivals without bookings after hauliers began receiving an additional booking reminder in August. Unbooked arrivals fell from 412 in August to 267 in September. The authority asks drivers to check the container release status before travelling, as a gate booking alone does not confirm that cargo is ready for collection.

Rail signalling fault delays inland container departures today

Ellis Corven 13 Oct 2026

A signalling fault at Reedbank Junction interrupted freight rail access to the Port of Kestrel Bay today. The junction operator stopped movements at 06:25 after a track detection circuit failed. Three outbound trains carrying a combined 144 containers were held in the port rail yard.

One train was bound for Amberford and two for the Saltmarsh inland terminal. The line reopened at 13:40 following replacement of the faulty component and a test movement. The first delayed train left the port at 14:05. No containers were transferred to road transport during the closure.

Rail customers received revised departure details through their booking contacts. Containers held on the affected trains have been exempted from additional port storage charges caused by the interruption. Vessel loading and unloading continued throughout the incident, and freight gates remained open. The fault occurred outside the port boundary and did not affect the terminal's internal rail equipment.

Berth Four fully reopens after quay repairs finish

Nina Halden 15 Oct 2026

Berth Four returned to its full working length of 305 metres today after the final repaired section passed inspection. Work began on 2 September and covered six mooring bollards, eight fenders and the concrete around the bollard foundations. The temporary fencing has been removed.

The completed work cost KRN 8.1 million against an allocation of KRN 8.4 million. The total includes engineering inspections, load tests and disposal of removed materials. Engineers signed off the final three bollards yesterday, and terminal staff completed checks of lighting and quay access before reopening the section.

Both container services temporarily reassigned to Berth Two are now back at Berth Four. Shipping agents have received the updated berth plan. The authority has also closed the temporary pedestrian diversion behind the works. Port users can use the usual marked walkway, while access to the quay edge remains restricted to authorised staff.

Port clears delayed vessel queue after fog restrictions

Ellis Corven 22 Oct 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay cleared its delayed vessel queue at 15:30 today after dense fog restricted harbour movements overnight. Visibility at the outer entrance fell below 200 metres, and vessel movements were suspended from 23:10 yesterday until 07:45 today. Five arriving vessels were held at the designated anchorage.

Harbour staff resumed movements after visibility improved and patrol crews checked the entrance channel. Departing vessels moved first where this released an occupied berth. Two container vessels, two general cargo ships and one coastal tanker then entered under revised arrival slots agreed with their agents.

Cargo work continued on vessels already alongside during the restriction. Freight gates and rail services operated normally, although collection times changed for some containers aboard the delayed arrivals. Customers can check release status through their usual account record. No collisions, groundings or injuries were reported during the fog restriction or the clearance of the queue.

New bilingual freight guidance supports Val-Brume cargo customers

Tomas Bellwick 19 Oct 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay has published freight collection guidance in English and French following requests from cargo customers in Val-Brume. The guidance covers gate bookings, container release checks, driver identification and the documents needed to collect goods through an appointed haulier.

Customers with billing addresses in the French-speaking region accounted for 12 per cent of loaded import collections during the first nine months of this year. The port's customer team reviewed 160 enquiries from those customers when preparing the guidance. Missing release references and uncertainty about collection authority were the most common problems.

Both language versions are available from the freight desk and in the customer account area. Printed copies carry the same numbered steps so staff and drivers can refer to the same instruction. The guidance explains existing procedures and introduces no additional documents or charges. Customers can request help from a French-speaking member of the customer team.

Ostara workshop helps manufacturers check labels before printing

Media centre · Elise Marvaux
21 September

Thirty-four staff from 22 food businesses attended a label checking workshop in Ostara, organised by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The session focused on common errors that can be caught before packaging goes to print.

Participants worked through fictional product labels covering soups, baked goods and chilled meals. Exercises included checking ingredient order, matching declared weights to product specifications and making storage instructions easy to find.

Elise Marvaux, technical affairs manager, said: “A second check against the recipe and specification can prevent an expensive reprint. Staff need a clear process for recording who approved a label and which version was sent to the printer.”

The federation distributed a two-page checklist and a sample approval record. The materials reflect current requirements and identify matters still under consultation in the draft labelling guidance. French versions are available to members through the federation’s advice service in Val-Brume.

Summer survey shows steady orders but tighter margins

Media centre · Tomas Bellan
1 September

Food manufacturers reported steady summer orders but continued pressure on margins, according to a survey published today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The survey received responses from 84 businesses employing 12,600 people.

Forty-six per cent said their order volumes were broadly unchanged from the previous three months. Thirty-one per cent reported an increase and 23 per cent a decline. Responses were collected between 10 and 24 August.

Packaging and maintenance were the most frequently reported sources of higher costs. Fifty-eight per cent of respondents said their operating margin had narrowed, while 37 per cent had postponed at least one planned equipment purchase.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Stable orders are welcome, but they do not mean every business is comfortable. Manufacturers in Amberford and Kestrel Bay described particular difficulty finding affordable replacement parts.” The federation cautioned that the voluntary survey represents participating members rather than the entire sector.

North freight gate reopens after overnight equipment fault

Ellis Corven 26 Aug 2026

The north freight gate at the Port of Kestrel Bay reopened at 09:20 today after a fault in its vehicle recognition equipment. The gate closed at 02:15. Freight traffic used the south entrance while technicians replaced a damaged power unit and checked the control system.

A total of 186 lorry bookings were affected. Drivers with valid bookings were admitted through the south gate without making a second booking, and the authority waived missed-slot charges linked to the closure. The longest recorded queue was 38 vehicles shortly before 07:00. No injuries or damage to cargo were reported.

Both freight entrances are now operating normally. Drivers whose booking records still show a missed visit can ask the gate office to correct the entry, quoting their vehicle registration and booking number. The fault did not affect rail movements, vessel operations or access to the empty-container yard.

Maintenance vacancies remain hardest to fill in autumn survey

Media centre · Tomas Bellan
9 October

Maintenance roles remain the hardest vacancies for food manufacturers to fill, according to a staffing survey released today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. Seventy-six member businesses responded between 22 September and 2 October.

Among the 49 respondents recruiting during that period, 29 reported difficulty hiring maintenance staff. Twenty-one reported difficulty recruiting machine operators. Businesses could select more than one role, so the figures do not represent separate groups of employers.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Employers described a shortage of applicants with experience of fault finding and routine equipment care. Several businesses in Kestrel Bay said vacancies had increased their reliance on external repair services.”

Thirty-two respondents said they had increased internal training during the previous six months. The federation is using the findings in discussions with training providers in Amberford and Ostara. The survey did not measure the effect of the proposed wage settlement announced this week.

Packaging levy revision removes duplicate reporting for manufacturers

Media centre · Mara Vennick
17 September

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has welcomed a revised packaging levy proposal published today by the Ministry of Revenue. The revision provides for one reporting return and removes a provision that could have counted some packaging twice.

The proposed rate remains KRN 0.18 per kilogram for the materials covered. The ministry has also added examples showing how manufacturers should record packaging purchased through wholesalers and packaging transferred between factories.

Mara Vennick, policy director, said: “These changes address a practical problem raised in our submission. Businesses can now assess the proposal with a clearer understanding of what they would need to report.”

The federation continues to seek clarification on reusable transport containers and the treatment of returned goods. It has asked members to submit examples with weights and purchase records. The levy remains a proposal, and the federation advises businesses to distinguish the draft requirements from their existing reporting duties.

Employers and union reach proposed sector wage settlement

Media centre · Devran Pell
7 October

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria and the Food Production Workers Union have reached a proposed sector wage settlement following negotiations in Saltmarsh. The proposal is subject to approval by participating employers and union members.

The settlement would raise the adult production minimum from KRN 14.20 to KRN 14.85 an hour. It also provides for a 4 per cent increase in shift allowances and eight hours of paid job-related training per covered employee each year.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “The proposed agreement recognises the pressure on household budgets while giving employers a clear basis for planning. The training provision also addresses a shared concern about progression within factories.”

The federation has circulated the full terms to all 63 participating employers. Existing contractual rates above the sector minimum are addressed separately in the document. Current terms remain in force while the approval process takes place.

The new food manufacturing sector wage agreement has been approved by participating employers and members of the Food Production Workers Union. The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria confirmed the result after both approval processes concluded.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “Approval gives payroll teams and employees certainty about the new terms. Our immediate priority is helping employers apply them correctly.” The federation has issued an implementation checklist covering payroll changes, staff notices and training records.

New labelling guidance needs clearer examples for small producers

Media centre · Elise Marvaux
3 September

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has asked the Food Standards Office to expand its draft guidance on ingredient labelling. Members say the document leaves uncertainty about how to display ingredients used within prepared fillings and sauces.

The federation reviewed 42 sample labels supplied by 18 manufacturers. Its technical team identified three recurring questions: where to place ingredient brackets, how to describe mixed oils and when a change in recipe requires revised packaging.

Elise Marvaux, technical affairs manager, said: “A bakery in Val-Brume should be able to reach the same answer as a sauce maker in Ostara. Clear examples would reduce mistakes and unnecessary calls for advice.”

The federation has submitted six worked examples and requested guidance in both Kestrian and French. It also recommends allowing businesses to use existing compliant packaging stocks when the change concerns presentation alone, provided all required consumer information remains accurate and legible.

Wage talks open with focus on pay and training

Media centre · Devran Pell
9 September

Negotiations on Kestria’s next food manufacturing sector wage agreement opened in Saltmarsh today. The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria is representing 63 employers covered by the agreement, alongside representatives of the Food Production Workers Union.

The opening meeting covered basic pay, shift allowances and access to paid training. The current agreement provides a minimum hourly rate of KRN 14.20 for adult production workers at participating businesses.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “We want an agreement that improves pay and helps factories retain skilled people. Employers also need to understand the full cost, including allowances, before they can make a firm commitment.”

Both negotiating teams exchanged evidence on vacancies, staff turnover and business costs. No pay settlement was reached at the opening meeting. The federation has asked participating employers to check their payroll information so that further discussions use consistent figures for hours, grades and shift patterns.

Media centre · Mara Vennick
28 August

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has called for changes to a proposed packaging levy, saying the current draft would require manufacturers to report the same material more than once.

In its submission to the Ministry of Revenue, the federation supports charging by packaging weight but asks for a single reporting return. The proposal sets a rate of KRN 0.18 per kilogram for certain packaging materials.

A review of records from 26 member businesses found that 19 would need to change their stock systems under the draft rules. Smaller manufacturers estimated an average initial cost of KRN 8,400, excluding staff time.

Mara Vennick, the federation’s policy director, said: “Members need clear definitions and a practical way to submit figures. One return, with worked examples, would help businesses meet the rules and make the information easier to check.”

Exchange extends afternoon trading for all agricultural futures

Notice No. 2026/341 · Category: Contracts

Date of issue: 28.09.2026 · Effective: 12.10.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has extended its regular trading session by 30 minutes. From today, wheat, oat and rapeseed futures trade from 08:30 to 16:30, using the exchange clock in Ostara. The opening time is unchanged. Members can enter orders during the pre-opening period from 08:15.

The daily settlement calculation now uses eligible trading activity between 16:20 and 16:30. Where activity is insufficient, the exchange applies its existing rules for assessing bids, offers and related contract months. The longer session responds to requests from members handling afternoon warehouse confirmations in Amberford and freight arrangements through Kestrel Bay.

Orders marked to expire at the end of the trading day now remain active until 16:30 unless cancelled or filled. Orders carrying a specific expiry time retain that instruction. Federation publishes costing guide for proposed wage agreement

Media centre · Devran Pell
12 October

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has published a costing guide to help participating employers assess the proposed sector wage agreement. The guide accompanies the settlement terms circulated on 7 October.

Worked examples cover basic pay, shift allowances and paid training time. For an employee working 38 paid hours a week at the adult production minimum, the proposed hourly increase of KRN 0.65 would add KRN 24.70 to weekly basic pay.

The guide explains that this figure excludes overtime, allowances and employer contributions. It also asks businesses to account for training cover where production duties need to be reassigned during an employee’s eight annual paid training hours.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “Employers need to assess the whole agreement using their own staffing patterns. These examples provide a common starting point.” The proposal remains subject to approval, and the guide does not replace the full settlement document or individual employment contracts.

Notice No. 2026/306 · Category: Trading hours

Date of issue: 18.08.2026 · Effective: 25.08.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has published a revised delivery guide for its wheat and oat futures. The guide brings warehouse instructions, sampling rules and delivery forms into one document. It applies to delivery notices submitted from today and does not change the quantity represented by either contract.

The guide also explains how warehouse charges are divided when ownership changes. Storage remains the seller's responsibility through the transfer date, with the buyer responsible from the following day. Members can obtain the guide through the exchange's document service. Trading resumes after morning interruption to order entry

Notice No. 2026/362 · Category: Trading hours

Date of issue: 08.10.2026 · Effective: 15.10.2026

Trading in wheat, oat and rapeseed futures resumed at 10:05 today after an interruption to the exchange's order entry service. Ostara Commodities Exchange suspended matching at 09:12 when monitoring identified delays in order acknowledgements. A ten-minute period for members to review and cancel orders preceded the reopening.

Trades completed before the suspension remain valid. Orders that had been accepted and remained unfilled were retained with their original priority. Messages that did not receive an acceptance acknowledgement were not added to the order book. Members were asked to reconcile their records against the exchange's order and trade reports before entering replacement instructions.

Technical staff traced the interruption to a fault in a message queue and moved the service to reserve equipment. The regular 16:30 closing time remains in place. Clearing and warehouse reporting services continued to operate during the interruption. The exchange is reviewing system records and member reports to establish why the fault was not resolved automatically.

Notice No. 2026/320 · Category: Margins

Date of issue: 26.08.2026 · Effective: 02.09.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has reduced the minimum price movement for oat futures from KRN 0.50 to KRN 0.25 per tonne. The change took effect at today's opening and applies to all listed delivery months. With a contract size of 20 tonnes, each minimum movement is now worth KRN 5.

Orders entered before the change remain valid because prices quoted in half-crown increments also meet the new quarter-crown requirement. Contract quantities, delivery standards and the method used to calculate daily settlement prices have not changed.

Members should check that their order systems accept prices ending in .25 and .75, as well as .00 and .50. The exchange's test service includes sample orders using each permitted ending. Clearing members must meet any resulting collateral shortfall by 09:00 on the next trading day. Eligible collateral and payment instructions are unchanged. Rapeseed delivery rules clarify sampling and retained records

Notice No. 2026/369 · Category: Contracts

Date of issue: 14.10.2026 · Effective: 28.10.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has issued a clarification of the sampling procedure for rapeseed delivered against its futures contracts. From today, delivery inspection records must state the sampling time, lot reference and seal numbers for retained samples. The clarification applies at every warehouse approved to handle exchange rapeseed deliveries.

Inspectors must prepare three sealed samples from each delivery lot: one for the seller, one for the buyer and one held by the warehouse. The warehouse sample must be retained for 45 calendar days after ownership transfers. Where a quality dispute remains open, it must be retained until the exchange confirms that the case is closed.

The maximum moisture content remains 9 per cent, and the maximum foreign matter allowance remains 2 per cent. Contract size and approved delivery locations are unchanged. Members can obtain the revised inspection form in English or French. Forms already completed for transferred lots remain valid; warehouses are not required to reopen completed deliveries solely to add the new record fields.

Val-Brume pension clinic offers support with annual returns

Written by Celia Bramwell

Trustees and employers in the Val-Brume area can now book free appointments at a pension reporting clinic on 8 October. Staff from the Pensions Oversight Authority will explain common annual return requirements and help visitors identify information missing from their records. Appointments will be available in French and English.

The clinic will take place at the Authority's Val-Brume office, with 36 appointments lasting 25 minutes each. Visitors should bring their plan registration number and a list of questions. They should not bring members' identity documents, bank details or individual medical records. Telephone appointments are available for those unable to attend.

The service follows a review of 94 returns from plans administered in the region. The most frequent errors concerned membership totals and changes to trustee contact details. Staff can explain reporting requirements but cannot complete returns for applicants or provide investment advice. Booking closes on 5 October, unless all appointments are filled earlier.

Annual report records faster action on unpaid pension contributions

Written by Mara Ellwick

The Pensions Oversight Authority's annual report, published today, records KRN 6.8 million in overdue employer contributions recovered following its intervention during the year ended 31 March 2026. The payments reached 73 workplace pension plans covering 18,420 members. Recoveries totalled KRN 5.1 million in the previous reporting year.

The median time from opening a contribution case to securing payment fell from 47 to 34 working days. The Authority issued 29 financial penalties and required improvements to record keeping at 61 plans. These figures cover completed cases; they do not include money still being pursued at the year end.

Operating expenditure was KRN 24.6 million against a budget of KRN 25.2 million. The report includes audited accounts, service measures and a breakdown of complaints about the Authority. Priorities for the current year include earlier checks on missed payments and clearer guidance for employers running smaller workplace plans.

Consultation opens on clearer recovery plans for underfunded pensions

Written by Tomas Vennick

The Pensions Oversight Authority is seeking views on proposed changes to the information employers and trustees provide when a workplace pension plan is underfunded. The consultation opens today and closes on 30 October. The proposals concern plans that promise members a set retirement income.

Under the proposals, recovery plans would explain why the payment schedule is affordable, what would happen if trading weakened and how trustees would monitor progress. A standard summary would show annual contributions in KRN alongside the expected funding shortfall. The Authority is also asking whether smaller plans need a shorter reporting form.

No funding rules change today. Existing recovery plans and payment schedules remain in force. Employers, trustees, advisers and members can respond through the Authority's consultation service or by post to its Saltmarsh office. An accompanying paper includes worked examples for a manufacturer, a transport business and a community services employer.

Amberford employer fined after repeated delays to pension contributions

Written by Leila Corven

The Pensions Oversight Authority has fined Amberford employer Brindle Quay Components KRN 42,000 after it repeatedly paid workplace pension contributions late. The company missed payment deadlines in seven months between September 2025 and April 2026. The delays affected 286 members of its workplace pension plan.

The employer has now paid the outstanding KRN 193,400, together with KRN 8,760 to compensate the plan for lost investment income. The fine is separate from those payments and must be paid by the company. It cannot be taken from pension assets or charged to members.

The Authority issued its final decision after considering the company's response to an earlier notice. The company has 28 days to appeal. Trustees have been asked to check contributions each month and report further delays. Members do not need to submit individual claims to receive the compensation within the plan.

Exchange completes review of order entry service interruption

Notice No. 2026/376 · Category: Margins

Date of issue: 15.10.2026 · Effective: 22.10.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has completed its review of the order entry interruption on 8 October. The review found that a software fault caused an internal message queue to stop releasing acknowledgements promptly. Automatic recovery did not start because the monitoring check measured connection availability without checking whether messages were progressing through the queue.

The exchange has added a separate check for message progress and tested the transfer to reserve equipment under simulated delays. It has also revised the procedure used by technical staff to confirm that order entry is ready to reopen. These changes are in operation. The review found no alteration to completed trade records.

Reconciliation with clearing members is complete, and no unresolved differences remain between accepted orders and the exchange's records for the affected period. Members can request their own message logs through the support service. The exchange has published a technical incident note setting out the interruption times, the cause and the checks applied before trading resumed.

Exchange introduces calendar spread orders for wheat futures

Notice No. 2026/390 · Category: Trading hours

Date of issue: 23.10.2026 · Effective: 30.10.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has introduced calendar spread orders for wheat futures. Members can now submit a single order to buy one listed wheat delivery month and sell another in equal quantities. The service is available during the regular 08:30 to 16:30 session and uses the same contract specifications as outright wheat trading.

Spread prices represent the price of the later delivery month minus the price of the earlier month, quoted in KRN per tonne. The minimum price movement is KRN 0.25 per tonne, equivalent to KRN 5 for a spread covering one 20-tonne contract in each month. Both sides execute together, removing the need to submit two separate outright orders.

Completed spreads create a separate futures position in each delivery month. Existing delivery obligations and position limits continue to apply to those positions. The exchange's published margin schedule determines the collateral required, including any eligible offset between months. Members can access worked examples and test messages through the document and test services. Oat and rapeseed order types are unchanged.

Market Operations, Ostara Commodities Exchange

Workplace pension funding improves in second quarter review

Written by Mara Ellwick

The Pensions Oversight Authority estimates that workplace pension plans promising a set retirement income held assets equal to 104 per cent of their liabilities at the end of June. This compares with 102 per cent at the end of March. The review covers 842 plans across Kestria, with combined assets of KRN 186 billion.

The improvement mainly reflects higher investment income and employer contributions. Funding remains uneven: 176 plans held less than the estimated amount needed to meet their promises. A national average does not show whether an individual plan can pay every benefit when it falls due.

Employers and trustees should continue making scheduled payments and reviewing their funding assumptions. The figures are estimates based on quarterly returns, rather than full valuations of every plan. The Authority has published regional tables, including separate results for Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume.

Kestrel Bay trustees directed to replace incomplete pension records

Written by Leila Corven

The Pensions Oversight Authority has directed the trustees of the Merehaven Packaging Retirement Plan in Kestrel Bay to repair incomplete membership records. An inspection found missing service dates or pay histories for 417 of the plan's 2,860 members. These records are needed to calculate promised retirement benefits accurately.

The trustees must produce a costed repair programme within 30 days and complete the work by 31 March 2027. They must also arrange an independent check of corrected records and send monthly progress reports to the Authority. The direction follows an earlier request for improvements that was not completed.

The inspection did not find evidence that assets were missing. Existing pension payments will continue, and the administrator will contact members if it needs information from them. Members should retain old benefit statements and employment records where available. The trustees have 28 days to appeal against the direction.

Trustees asked to check member addresses before annual statements

Written by Celia Bramwell

The Pensions Oversight Authority is asking workplace pension trustees to check their member contact records before issuing annual benefit statements this autumn. A review of 120 plans found that 8.4 per cent of statements sent during the previous reporting cycle were returned or could not be delivered electronically.

Plans should compare their records with recent updates from members and employers, investigate returned post and provide a straightforward way to correct an address. Trustees should take particular care with former employees who still hold benefits in the plan. An employer's current payroll list will not necessarily include these members.

The Authority has published a short checklist covering address checks, secure identity verification and records of delivery failures. Members who have moved should contact their pension administrator using details from an existing statement. They should never be asked to pay a fee simply to update their postal or email address.

Written by Celia Bramwell

The Pensions Oversight Authority has published additional annual return guidance following its reporting clinic in Val-Brume on 8 October. Staff held 34 appointments with employers and trustees, including nine by telephone. Most questions concerned how to count members who had left employment but retained pension benefits.

The updated guidance explains how to report contributing members, members with benefits left in a plan and members already receiving a pension. The examples are available in French and English and can be used by plans throughout Kestria. They clarify existing requirements and do not introduce new categories. Plans that have already submitted a return should check the guidance and contact the Authority if they identify a material error. Routine contact changes can be submitted through the usual update service.

Third quarter figures show fewer unresolved pension payment reports

Written by Mara Ellwick

There were 64 unresolved reports of late workplace pension contributions at 30 September, down from 81 at 30 June, according to figures published today by the Pensions Oversight Authority. The figures count reports under investigation and do not represent every late payment across Kestria.

The Authority received 147 new reports during the third quarter and closed 164. Of the closed reports, 139 ended with full payment, 17 concerned reporting errors and eight were combined with existing investigations. Reports can cover several missed payments by the same employer, so case numbers should not be read as employer totals.

Among the unresolved reports, 12 had been open for more than 90 days. These included disputed payroll records and employers experiencing financial difficulty. Trustees should continue pursuing unpaid contributions while an investigation is open. Reporting a delay to the Authority does not transfer responsibility for collecting payments from the plan's trustees.

Ostara employer agrees repayment schedule for outstanding pension contributions

Written by Leila Corven

The Pensions Oversight Authority has accepted an enforceable undertaking from Ostara employer Tarnwick Cold Stores to repay KRN 724,000 in outstanding workplace pension contributions. The arrears relate to employer contributions due between February and July 2026 and affect 612 members. Contributions deducted from employees' pay were paid to the plan.

The company paid KRN 224,000 on 19 October. The remaining KRN 500,000 must be paid in five monthly instalments, beginning on 20 November, alongside all new contributions as they fall due. The company must also pay compensation for lost investment income, calculated under the terms of the undertaking.

Trustees will confirm receipt of each payment directly to the Authority. If the employer breaches the undertaking, the Authority can seek a court order requiring compliance. Members will receive a written update from the plan administrator. Acceptance of the undertaking does not mean the arrears have been cleared.

Employers given clearer steps for reporting late pension payments

Written by Tomas Vennick

The Pensions Oversight Authority has published guidance explaining how employers and trustees should report late workplace pension contributions. It includes examples covering payroll errors, missing payment references and repeated delays. The guidance applies to reports made from today and does not change the legal payment deadlines.

Trustees should record when a payment was due, the amount outstanding and the steps taken to recover it. Where a report is required, it should distinguish money deducted from staff pay from contributions owed by the employer. Employers should give trustees a named contact who can resolve payment queries.

During the first six months of 2026, the Authority received 318 reports involving late payments. Of these, 241 were resolved within 20 working days of the initial report. The new guidance includes a reporting checklist and sample payment record, with versions available in English and French.

One week remains to comment on pension recovery proposals

Written by Tomas Vennick

Employers, trustees and pension members have until 30 October to respond to the Pensions Oversight Authority's consultation on recovery plans for underfunded workplace pensions. The consultation opened on 14 September. It proposes clearer explanations of payment schedules, business risks and the steps trustees would take if a recovery plan fell behind.

By 22 October, the Authority had received 68 responses, including 21 from employers and 14 from trustee boards. Responses received so far raise questions about the work required of smaller plans and how employers should describe uncertain future income. The Authority has added answers to procedural questions to its consultation page.

Respondents can answer individual questions without completing the whole document. They should identify any information they consider confidential and explain why. Existing funding requirements remain in place while the proposals are considered. The Authority will review submissions after the closing date and publish its response before setting any implementation timetable.

New guidance explains pension duties when employers change payroll

Written by Tomas Vennick

Employers changing payroll systems should test pension deductions before the first live pay run, according to guidance published today by the Pensions Oversight Authority. The guidance addresses errors involving contribution rates, pensionable pay and the transfer of employee records. It applies to employers of all sizes.

The Authority reviewed 52 contribution incidents linked to payroll changes between January and August 2026. In 31 cases, an incorrect setting was copied across a whole group of employees. The guidance recommends checking sample calculations, agreeing payment references with the pension administrator and confirming who will investigate any mismatch.

Changing a payroll provider does not change an employer's responsibility to pay contributions in full and on time. Employers should keep a record of checks and explain corrections clearly to affected staff. The publication includes examples for weekly and monthly payrolls, together with a handover checklist that can be shared with payroll providers.

Le crédit régional simplifie la déclaration des dépenses admissibles

Par Lucien Dorselin

Publié le 1er septembre 2026 · Mis à jour le 7 septembre 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume met aujourd’hui en service un formulaire simplifié pour le crédit régional à l’investissement productif. Les entreprises peuvent désormais regrouper leurs dépenses d’équipement dans un seul tableau. Cette modification réduit le nombre de pièces à remplir, sans changer le taux du crédit ni les critères d’admissibilité.

Le crédit correspond à 12 % des dépenses reconnues, jusqu’à concurrence de 240 000 KRN par entreprise et par exercice. Le nouveau tableau distingue le prix d’achat, les frais d’installation et les autres aides reçues. Il comporte aussi une case pour signaler un équipement partagé entre plusieurs établissements, une situation qui demandait auparavant une note séparée.

La révision s’appuie sur un essai réalisé en juillet avec 18 entreprises et six cabinets de tenue de livres. Le temps médian de préparation observé est passé de 95 à 62 minutes. Les demandes déjà déposées demeurent valides. L’Agence n’exige pas leur transcription dans le nouveau formulaire et poursuit leur traitement selon leur date de réception.

Douze entreprises reçoivent une aide pour leurs diagnostics énergétiques

Par Élodie Mireval

Publié le 28 août 2026 · Mis à jour le 4 septembre 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume accorde une aide totale de 216 000 KRN à douze entreprises dans le cadre du volet Diagnostic énergétique. Ces contributions soutiennent l’examen des systèmes de chauffage, de ventilation et de production. Les entreprises retenues emploient ensemble 287 personnes dans cinq localités de la région.

Parmi les bénéficiaires, les Séchoirs de Brumecôte obtiennent 24 000 KRN pour mesurer les pertes de chaleur de leurs installations. La Menuiserie des Trois-Vernes reçoit 16 500 KRN pour analyser sa consommation d’électricité. Les montants accordés couvrent la moitié des honoraires admissibles, selon la portée de chaque diagnostic et les soumissions déposées.

Les conventions d’aide ont toutes été signées. Le versement des contributions exige un rapport technique et des factures acquittées. Aucune économie d’énergie n’est comptabilisée à cette étape : le diagnostic sert à établir les possibilités d’amélioration. Une entreprise qui souhaite ensuite financer des équipements doit présenter une demande distincte au programme correspondant.

Un comptoir supplémentaire pour accompagner les entreprises de Rive-des-Ormes

Par Bastien Corvelin

Publié le 27 août 2026 · Mis à jour le 2 septembre 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume a ouvert aujourd’hui un comptoir de services à Rive-des-Ormes, dans la maison régionale des métiers. Deux conseillères y accompagnent les entreprises dans la préparation de leurs demandes de subvention et de crédit d’impôt. Ce point de service dessert aussi les secteurs voisins de Clairvallon et du Hameau-des-Saules.

Le comptoir dispose de trois espaces de consultation, dont un bureau fermé pour les échanges confidentiels. Son aménagement a nécessité un investissement de 86 000 KRN, payé à même le budget de fonctionnement de l’Agence. Les services sont gratuits. Les entreprises peuvent prendre rendez-vous par téléphone ou demander une première orientation directement à l’accueil.

L’équipe aide notamment à vérifier les dépenses admissibles au programme Atelier durable, ouvert le 21 août. Elle peut aussi expliquer les pièces à joindre aux demandes existantes. L’ouverture de ce comptoir répond à une consultation menée en juin auprès de 74 entreprises, dont 46 avaient signalé des difficultés de déplacement vers Val-Brume.

Une enveloppe régionale pour moderniser les petits ateliers

Par Maëlle Vardelin

Publié le 21 août 2026 · Mis à jour le 23 août 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume annonce aujourd’hui une enveloppe de 3,6 millions de couronnes kestrianes (KRN) pour la modernisation des petits ateliers de la région. Le programme Atelier durable est ouvert aux entreprises comptant de 3 à 49 personnes. Il vise le remplacement d’équipements usés, la réduction des pertes de matières et l’amélioration des postes de travail.

L’aide couvre jusqu’à 35 % des dépenses admissibles, pour un maximum de 180 000 KRN par entreprise. Les projets doivent représenter un investissement d’au moins 40 000 KRN. Les achats effectués avant le dépôt d’une demande ne sont pas admissibles. Chaque dossier doit comprendre deux soumissions et une description des gains attendus.

Les entreprises de Val-Brume, de Rive-des-Ormes et de Mont-des-Filons peuvent obtenir un accompagnement gratuit auprès de l’Agence. Le formulaire et le guide du programme sont accessibles dès aujourd’hui sur son site. Une version imprimée est également disponible au comptoir d’accueil de Val-Brume.

Un premier bilan des demandes au programme Atelier durable

Par Bastien Corvelin

Publié le 17 septembre 2026

Depuis l’ouverture du programme Atelier durable le 21 août, l’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume a reçu 43 demandes représentant 2,1 millions de KRN d’aide sollicitée. De ce nombre, 31 dossiers contiennent toutes les pièces nécessaires à leur analyse. Les douze autres nécessitent des renseignements complémentaires, principalement des soumissions détaillées.

Les demandes proviennent de huit localités. Elles concernent surtout le travail du bois, la fabrication de pièces et la réparation d’équipements. À ce jour, aucune contribution n’a été accordée. Le montant demandé ne constitue donc pas un engagement de l’Agence et ne doit pas être interprété comme une somme déjà versée aux entreprises.

L’enveloppe du programme demeure de 3,6 millions de KRN. Pour faciliter l’analyse, l’Agence rappelle que chaque soumission doit préciser le modèle d’équipement, son prix et les frais d’installation. Les entreprises peuvent compléter leur dossier avec l’aide des équipes de Val-Brume ou de Rive-des-Ormes. Une demande d’information auprès d’un conseiller ne réserve aucune portion de l’enveloppe.

Un soutien de proximité pour les commerces de Clairvallon

Par Maëlle Vardelin

Publié le 10 septembre 2026

Neuf commerces de Clairvallon bénéficient d’un soutien total de 342 000 KRN pour adapter leurs locaux et améliorer leur fonctionnement. L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume a confirmé ces aides dans le cadre du programme Commerce de proximité. Les investissements admissibles des entreprises totalisent 855 000 KRN.

Les projets comprennent l’installation de portes accessibles, le remplacement de chambres froides et l’aménagement de zones de préparation de commandes. L’Épicerie des Aulnes reçoit notamment 48 000 KRN pour réorganiser sa réserve et remplacer deux appareils de réfrigération. La Maison du Fil de Brume obtient 21 000 KRN pour adapter son entrée et son espace de service.

Chaque contribution représente 40 % des dépenses reconnues. Les travaux de décoration et les achats destinés à la revente sont exclus. Les commerces retenus comptent ensemble 61 emplois, mais les conventions ne présentent pas ce nombre comme une création d’emplois. Le suivi porte sur les factures, la réalisation des aménagements approuvés et le maintien de l’activité dans les locaux concernés.

Publié le 6 octobre 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume confirme les sept premières contributions du programme Atelier durable, pour un total de 924 000 KRN. Les projets approuvés représentent des investissements de 2,8 millions de KRN. Ils concernent quatre entreprises de Val-Brume, deux de Mont-des-Filons et une de Rive-des-Ormes.

Les Ateliers du Haut-Saule reçoivent 168 000 KRN pour remplacer une ligne de découpe et installer un système de récupération des chutes. À Mont-des-Filons, Mécanique Brumacier obtient 126 000 KRN pour acquérir deux appareils d’usinage. Les évaluations techniques jointes aux dossiers décrivent les gains attendus; ceux-ci restent à vérifier après la mise en service.

Ces décisions portent sur des demandes complètes examinées depuis le bilan du 17 septembre. Les sommes annoncées sont engagées dans les conventions, mais aucun remboursement final n’a encore été effectué. Les versements exigent des preuves d’achat et d’installation. L’Agence maintient une enveloppe de 3,6 millions de KRN pour l’ensemble du programme et poursuit l’analyse des autres dossiers reçus.

Les délais de traitement diminuent pour le crédit régional

Par Lucien Dorselin

Publié le 8 octobre 2026

Le délai médian de traitement des dossiers complets du crédit régional à l’investissement productif s’établit à 19 jours ouvrables en septembre, comparativement à 27 en août. L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume publie aujourd’hui cet indicateur avec le nombre de décisions rendues. Il mesure la période entre la réception d’un dossier complet et la transmission de la décision.

En septembre, l’Agence a rendu 38 décisions : 33 attestations favorables et cinq refus. Les dépenses reconnues dans les dossiers acceptés totalisent 8,4 millions de KRN, pour des crédits de 1 008 000 KRN. Les refus concernent des équipements non admissibles ou des dépenses engagées hors de la période couverte par le programme.

Le formulaire simplifié, offert depuis le 1er septembre, facilite la vérification des montants déclarés. Une réaffectation interne a aussi ajouté une personne à l’équipe d’analyse. Le délai publié n’est pas une garantie individuelle : les dossiers qui nécessitent des précisions peuvent demander davantage de temps. L’attestation de l’Agence ne constitue pas un versement de fonds.

Le rapport annuel détaille les aides et leurs résultats

Par Bastien Corvelin

Publié le 16 octobre 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume publie son rapport annuel pour l’exercice terminé le 30 juin 2026. Elle y présente 146 conventions de subvention totalisant 18,7 millions de KRN et 92 attestations de crédit d’impôt représentant 6,2 millions de KRN. Ces deux formes de soutien sont comptabilisées séparément dans les tableaux financiers.

Les conventions de subvention concernent 131 entreprises, certaines ayant obtenu une aide pour deux projets distincts. Parmi les 88 projets dont le suivi technique est terminé, 76 ont atteint tous les objectifs inscrits à leur convention. Huit les ont atteints en partie et quatre ont été abandonnés. Les sommes versées pour ces quatre projets ont été récupérées.

Le rapport comprend aussi les dépenses de fonctionnement de l’Agence, établies à 2,9 millions de KRN, ainsi que la répartition territoriale des aides. Les résultats reposent sur les factures, les visites et les déclarations vérifiées disponibles à la clôture. Le document et ses tableaux en format accessible sont offerts sur le site de l’Agence et à ses deux comptoirs.

Une aide ciblée pour six entreprises du Hameau-des-Saules

Par Maëlle Vardelin

Publié le 14 octobre 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume accorde 198 000 KRN à six entreprises du Hameau-des-Saules pour remettre en état des équipements endommagés par le refoulement du collecteur local du 30 septembre. Le soutien provient du fonds de continuité des petites entreprises. Les dossiers ont été examinés à partir des constats de dommages et des estimations de réparation.

L’aide couvre jusqu’à 50 % des dépenses admissibles qui ne sont pas remboursées par une assurance. Chaque entreprise doit déclarer les indemnités reçues. Les conventions prévoient un ajustement si une indemnité supplémentaire couvre une dépense déjà soutenue par l’Agence. Les pertes de ventes et la valeur des stocks détruits sont exclues de cette aide.

Les projets acceptés comprennent la réparation de moteurs, le nettoyage spécialisé d’installations et le remplacement de commandes électriques. Les six entreprises comptent 44 personnes à leur emploi. Deux ont déjà repris leurs activités dans leurs locaux. L’Agence accompagne les autres dans la préparation des pièces requises pour le remboursement des travaux autorisés.

Les ateliers de demande ont accompagné cinquante-deux entreprises régionales

Par Élodie Mireval

Publié le 21 octobre 2026 · Mis à jour le 25 octobre 2026

Cinquante-deux entreprises ont participé aux ateliers gratuits de préparation des demandes offerts par l’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume entre le 2 septembre et le 15 octobre. Les six séances, tenues à Val-Brume et à Rive-des-Ormes, ont réuni 67 personnes. Elles portaient sur les budgets de projet, les soumissions et les preuves de paiement.

Les exercices utilisaient des dossiers fictifs pour expliquer comment distinguer une dépense admissible d’une dépense courante. Une attention particulière a été accordée au cumul des subventions et des crédits d’impôt. Sur les 49 questionnaires remis, 41 indiquent que la séance a permis de corriger au moins une erreur dans un budget en préparation.

Le coût total des séances s’élève à 14 600 KRN, incluant les salles, les documents et le temps de préparation externe. Les fiches utilisées sont maintenant accessibles sur le site de l’Agence. La participation ne donne aucun avantage dans l’évaluation d’une demande. Les entreprises qui n’ont pas assisté aux séances peuvent obtenir les mêmes explications auprès d’un conseiller.

Une vérification précise les règles de cumul des aides

Par Lucien Dorselin

Publié le 22 octobre 2026

L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume publie une fiche explicative sur le cumul des aides après une vérification de 24 dossiers d’investissement. L’examen, terminé le 19 octobre, a relevé trois déclarations incomplètes concernant d’autres contributions publiques. Les entreprises concernées ont fourni les renseignements manquants. Les corrections représentent ensemble 37 200 KRN.

Dans deux dossiers, la correction a réduit un solde de subvention qui n’avait pas encore été versé. Dans le troisième, un remboursement de 8 400 KRN a été reçu le 20 octobre. La vérification n’a relevé aucune autre somme à récupérer dans l’échantillon examiné. Elle ne permet toutefois pas de conclure sur l’ensemble des dossiers de l’Agence.

La nouvelle fiche présente trois exemples chiffrés et indique où déclarer une subvention, un crédit d’impôt ou une aide remboursable. Les plafonds demeurent ceux de chaque programme. L’Agence rappelle qu’une même facture peut devoir être déclarée dans plusieurs formulaires, même lorsque les aides sont administrées par des équipes différentes. Les entreprises peuvent faire vérifier leur calcul avant de transmettre leur déclaration.
